LogoParamountPlus More live games and exclusives Log Out Connect TV Provider More live games & exclusives Log Out Connect NFL News & Highlights How to watch the 'Thursday Night Football' matchup, plus a preview and prediction Patrick Smith/Getty Images In the Week 10 edition of "Thursday Night Football," the New York Giants play host to the division rival Washington Commanders . New York enters this game riding high atop the NFC East, having won each of its last two games sandwiching a Week 8 bye. The Giants are surprisingly in the playoff picture in the first year of the John Harbaugh era despite losing starting quarterback Jaxson Dart in Week 2. They recently turned to J.J. McCarthy in place of Jameis Winston but kept on winning. Washington climbed out of last place in the NFC East thanks to a Week 8 win over the lowly Philadelphia Eagles but still has the second-worst record in the conference. The Commanders missed an opportunity for a win the last time these two teams played by mismanaging the clock as poorly as any team ever has, and they will surely be looking to atone for that mistake here. Will the Giants keep rolling, or will the Commanders capture a rare victory? We'll find out soon enough. Before we break down the matchup, here's a look at how you can watch the game. Where to watch Giants vs. Commanders live Date: Thursday, Nov. 12 | Time: 8:20 p.m. ET Location: MetLife Stadium (East Rutherford, New Jersey) Streaming: Amazon Prime Follow: CBS Sports App Odds: Giants -2.5, O/U 40.5 via DraftKings Sportsbook When the Commanders have the ball The Commanders are not particularly effective either passing or running the football. They rank 21st in the NFL in net yards per pass attempt (which accounts for yards lost to sacks), and they're 23rd in designed rushing yards per carry, which eliminates scrambling from the picture. Their most effective form of offense is scrambling, where Jayden Daniels and Marcus Mariota have run 29 times for 274 yards — the most scramble yards in the NFL, per Tru Media. But that's not something that you can lean on down-to-down. Daniels has completed only 63.9% of his passes at an average of 6.9 yards per attempt. While he has seven passing touchdowns and has yet to be intercepted, he has a low passing success rate (43.9%, according to Tru Media), has generated explosives at only an average rate (7.8%) and has struggled on third downs (30.9%). Again, his most effective way of moving the ball has been via the scramble. The Giants are actually second in the NFL in passing success rate allowed and third in explosives per dropback, according to Tru Media. So Daniels, with his limited receiving corps in the absence of Terry McLaurin , might find it difficult to move the ball through the air. The Giants, though, have been vulnerable to opponent scrambles, allowing quarterbacks to take off downfield on a league-high 23.9% of pressured dropbacks and yielding 225 scramble yards to date. So Daniels could have some room to run. In the absence of Jacory Croskey-Merritt , the Commies have turned to Rachaad White and Austin Ekeler in the backfield. They have not been particularly effective on the ground, but they're each capable outlet receivers for Daniels, who has targeted backs on 14.4% of his passes, a slightly higher rate than last year (12.8%). Doing so against the Giants may not be the most advisable strategy, though, because it means testing rookie linebacker Arvell Reese in space, and Reese has been a space-eating demon so far this season. Daniels' other pass-catchers at the moment are Stefon Diggs , Antonio Williams , Van Jefferson and Chig Okonkwo. The Giants have been good at limiting tight ends over the middle (there's Reese showing up again), so the passing game might run through the perimeter receivers, who will face off with an improved Deonte Banks and the recently-extended Greg Newsome II on the outside. Look for Daniels to at least try to test those guys deep down the field, given he has the seventh-highest deep throw rate among qualified quarterbacks. The Giants have faced deep passes at essentially an average rate so far this season, and they've been excellent at defending them, checking in second in EPA per dropback on those plays. Still, dinking and dunking hasn't been all that effective for Daniels and the Commanders, so they're going to have to try to hit on a few big plays. When the Giants have the ball The Giants turned to J.J. McCarthy as their quarterback in garbage time of their loss to the Saints back in Week 6, and they have stuck with him over the last two games. They've been a somewhat unusual offense with McCarthy under center. McCarthy himself has not been efficient on a down-to-down basis. He's completed only 63.2% of his passes, and he has one touchdown pass and one interception. He checks in 31st in success rate among 37 quarterbacks with at least 75 dropbacks this season, according to Tru Media. But McCarthy is averaging 9.1 (!!!!) yards per attempt, and he's 15th among the same group of 37 quarterbacks in EPA per dropback. That's because when he does complete passes, they're basically all going for big gains in big situations. He's throwing the ball farther downfield than anyone in the league (10.6-yard average depth of target), and he's leading the NFL in explosive plays per dropback at 16.0%, per Tru Media. The Commanders' defense is essentially the opposite of what McCarthy has done so far. They yield a high passing success rate (21st in the league) but a low explosive rate (11th). The tension between those two poles will be interesting to watch play out on Monday night. When McCarthy drops back to pass, he is looking most often to Malik Nabers , who has been the intended receiver on 31.7% of McCarthy's throws. Malachi Fields , not Isaiah Likely , has been the secondary target, with a 20.6% target share compared to Likely's 17.5% rate. Before McCarthy took over at quarterback, Likely tied Nabers for the team lead in target share at 29.4%, compared to just 11.2% for Fields. Nabers and Fields will do most of their work against Rasul Douglas and Amik Robertson on the outside, while Likely will see a lot of rookie linebacker Sonny Styles , slot corner Mike Sainristil and safeties Jeremy Reaves and Nick Cross . The Commanders have not generated very much pressure this season (33.5% of opponent dropbacks, per Tru Media, 25th in the league), while McCarthy has been one of the league's most-pressured quarterbacks since taking over. He tends to hold the ball for a while as he looks to push it down the field. Whether the Commanders can get after him will go a long way toward determining whether he can complete any big plays. Cam Skattebo is back for the Giants in this game, and he's likely to take over the lead role from Devin Singletary , who struggled last week and is more suited to being a passing-down back. Skattebo hasn't been very effective as a rusher this season, averaging 4.3 yards per carry with a 45.9% success rate, but he had his best game of the year before sitting out last week after the bye. The Commanders have been solid against the run, yielding only 3.9 yards per carry, with below-average marks both before (1.09) and after contact (2.83). This might be a game where the Giants lean on those big plays from McCarthy. I don't feel particularly comfortable predicting that this Giants team will improve to 6-2-1, but I just don't have much faith this version of Washington can be all that competitive either. The Commanders can't run the ball right now and have to lean on a passing game that hasn't been all that efficient. The Giants haven't exactly looked like world beaters this year (four of their five wins have come in one-score games), and they definitely didn't look great against the Eagles last week, but I think they can get it done on Thursday night. The former first-round pick has 78 targets in eight games, reeling in 53 passes for 648 yards and two scores. While he hasn’t found the end zone a bunch in 2026, Nabers has at least six grabs in five of his eight games and has four straight matchups with at least eight targets. He had a huge game against Washington earlier this season, pulling down 11 of his 20 targets for 121 yards and a score. The Commanders have struggled against the pass all season long, ranking 18th in the league in passing yards allowed while also allowing the sixth-most passing scores. I expect Nabers to be heavily involved in the game plan once again on Thursday night. Daniels torched the Giants on the ground in Week 5, rushing nine times for 103 yards and two scores. He has just two games this season with over 35.5 rushing yards, but Daniels has really killed the Giants on the ground in his NFL career. The star quarterback has 44, 35, 68 and 103 rushing yards in his four games against the division rival, and New York has given up the third-most rushing yards to the quarterback position in 2026. A lot of that is because of Daniels’ big game, but I like this matchup for the Commanders signal-caller on Thursday. New York has struggled to get home this season, posting the worst pressure rate in the NFL while picking up just 16 sacks in eight games. Even though the Giants are third in the NFL in success rate, they have shown that they can’t keep contain on Daniels, who is one of the best athletes in open space in the league. In the red zone, Likely has nine targets in 2026, turning those into eight catches and five touchdowns. He hasn’t missed a beat with the New York quarterback changes, finding the end zone in Weeks 1, 5, 6 and 9. Yes, he scored against Washington in the overtime matchup in Week 5, catching 11 of his 13 targets for 94 yards and two scores. The Commanders have allowed eight touchdown passes to opposing tight ends in 2026 – the second-most in the NFL. At nearly 2/1, Likely is a great bet to lead this Giants offense once again in Week 10. away.blurb: Commanders' Famous QB Could Replace Drake Maye for Patriots Unlock the latest Heavy on Commanders news — direct to your inbox. The Washington Commanders have a budding celebrity in quarterback Sam Hartman who can't get on the field for their franchise, but is a candidate for a shot with the New England Patriots before making his debut as a reality television star early next year. New England lost starting quarterback Drake Maye to an ankle injury against the Detroit Lions early in a Week 10 matchup in Munich, Germany. The issue is likely to sideline Maye for several weeks, if not the remainder of the campaign, based on the coming determination of its seriousness. NFL insider Jordan Schultz reported on Monday, November 16 that the Patriots are already seeking a QB addition given Maye's health concerns. Tommy DeVito is currently expected to become the "The #Patriots are expected to explore the QB market during the bye week, from free agents such as Jimmy Garoppolo, who has previously played for OC Josh McDaniels, to potentially adding a QB off another team's practice squad," Schultz posted to X . "Tommy DeVito is currently expected to become the starter." Sam Hartman Has Yet to Make Name for Himself as NFL QB Getty Washington Commanders quarterback Sam Hartman. Hartman, 27, has never played a snap in a regular-season NFL game. However, he played six years of college football, in part due to his presence at the collegiate level during the COVID-19 pandemic. He spent five years with Wake Forest before playing his final campaign at Notre Dame. Hartman threw for nearly 13,000 yards along with 110 TDs and 41 INTs across 48 games played at Wake Forest then tallied nearly 2,700 yards, 24 TDs and eight INTs during his 12-game run with the Fighting Irish. Hartman joined the Commanders in April of 2024 as an undrafted free agent and has spent the overwhelming majority of his time with the franchise (now in his third professional campaign) as a member of the practice squad. However, Washington did sign him to the active roster ahead of its Christmas Day game against the NFC East Division rival Dallas Cowboys last year. The Commanders started quarterback Josh Johnson in that contest, which they lost by a score of 30-23 at Northwest Stadium. And while Hartman suited up and watched from the sideline, he never got into the actual game. Sam Hartman to Star in ABC's ‘The Bachelor' Early Next Year While Hartman attained a modicum of fame as the quarterback of Notre Dame, which is among the handful of college football programs with a well-dispersed and plentiful fanbase that affords it a truly national reach, he is sure to find more fame as the star of ABC's coming season of "The Bachelor." The network recently announced Hartman's participation as its featured bachelor for the 30th season of the show, which will begin airing in March of 2027. Skip to main content Primary nav SEASON TICKETS Center Lucas Patrick and tight end Colson Yankoff have been ruled out for the Washington Commanders' game against the New York Giants on Thursday Night Football. It was essentially a foregone conclusion that Patrick would miss at least one game, which is why head coach Dan Quinn confirmed earlier in the week that veteran Nick Allegretti would be the starting center. Allegretti has dealt with multiple injuries since training camp that have limited his time on the field, but the Commanders are confident in his ability to direct their offensive line against a Giants defense that blitzes at the third-highest rate in the league. "I'm excited to feel good physically and get an opportunity to go out there," Allegretti said Tuesday. The Washington Commanders are taking on the New York Giants in Week 10. Check out this Gameday blog for stats, updates and more. Patrick was placed in the concussion protocol during the Commanders' game against the Los Angeles Rams. Yankoff is dealing with a knee injury that has hampered him since last week. Both were listed as non-participants all week. Allegretti, a seven-year veteran with 34 starts in 107 games, specialized at guard throughout his professional career prior to the 2026 season and even started at left guard for the Commanders during the entire 2024 season. He was relatively solid in that span, particularly as a pass protector. In 1,576 career pass blocking snaps, he allowed just five sacks and 13 quarterback hits. The Commanders have options at tight end outside of Yankoff, who only has three catches for 22 yards this season, but Yankoff is a key special teams contributor with 185 snaps running with the unit. The Commanders will need to find a temporary replacement for his production, but there are players like Jeremy Reaves and Ben Sinnott would could fill his role. LogoParamountPlus More live games and exclusives Log Out Connect TV Provider More live games & exclusives Log Out Connect NFL News & Highlights Everything you need to know to catch the game Imagn Images The New England Patriots and Detroit Lions will kick off Sunday's action with a 9:30 a.m. game at Allianz Arena in Munich, Germany on Sunday, Nov. 15. The Lions come into the international matchup at 6-2 and are coming off a 19-9 win over the Miami Dolphins . The victory extended their win streak to four games. Detroit's 6-2 record is strong, but because the NFC North is so good, they are currently narrowly in second place in the division, tied record-wise with the Minnesota Vikings . The Patriots story is a bit different, coming off a bad loss to the Green Bay Packers . In the 45-27 defeat, quarterback Drake Maye threw three interceptions, tying him with winless Los Angeles Chargers QB Justin Herbert for most picks in the league (11). The Patriots are 2-2 in their last four games and sit in second place in the AFC East. Both teams can make big plays, but it's what happens between those big gains that may determine the winner of this matchup between two coaches, Mike Vrabel and Dan Campbell, who tend to be aggressive in their play-calling. Lions vs. Patriots need to know Injuries: The Patriots will be without CB Carlton Davis III (knee), C/G Ben Brown (knee) and RB TreVeyon Henderson (illness) this week and nine other players are questionable, including WR A.J. Brown (ankle/knee), RB Rhamondre Stevenson (knee) and S Kevin Byard III (chest). Brown, who has missed the last two weeks and was IR earlier this season, returned to practice this week in a limited capacity. Brown's production in the three games he did play didn't live up to his hype, drawing criticism from fans. If he can play, all eyes will be on him, especially with the team having fewer options in the run game. Defenses: The Lions' defense has improved over the last few weeks, allowing 15.5 points per game in its last four matchups, after being near the bottom of the league in many categories, including yards allowed per game (423.8) in the first four weeks. The Patriots defense got embarrassed last week, with arguably Christian Gonzalez's worst game of his career. New England's defense has allowed the eighth most passing yards per game (231.9). The team does significantly better against the run, landing eighth-best (96.7), right behind the Lions' run defense (94.1). The Lions offense is top 10 in the league, thanks to Jaymyr Gibbs, who already has 847 yards on the ground and will present a challenge for the Patriots. The Lions' pass defense is still at the bottom in terms of yards allowed (260.9), and with the Patriots needing to improve and establish their air game, this would be the chance to try and expose Detroit's weakness. Pass game: The Patriots' passing game pales in comparison to their Week 10 opponent's. Lions wide receiver Amon-Ra St. Brown has 61 receptions for 657 receiving yards, more than the Patriots' top two WRs ( DeMario Douglas , Efton Chism III ) combined. The lack of production is in part due to struggles from quarterback Drake Maye and the absence of a true WR1, with Brown missing most games and the loss of Kayshon Boutte this offseason. St. Brown's mom is from Germany and it will be the first game he plays on German soil, which should only increase his excitement and production. International history: This marks the sixth regular-season game to be held in Germany and the third played in Munich. It marks the final European game of the season. The NFL traveled to Germany last season as well, when the Colts and Falcons met in November at the Olympic Stadium. Detroit Lions president & CEO Rod Wood expressed his excitement to be playing in Germany, saying , "We are thrilled to be playing internationally and specifically in Munich for the 2026 season. As an organization, we have invested greatly in the German market and are excited to play in front of our passionate German fans." Lions vs. Patriots where to watch Date: Sunday, Nov. 15 | Time: 9:30 a.m. ET Location : Allianz Arena (Munich, Germany) TV: Fox | Stream: fubo (free trial available) Follow: CBS Sports App Odds: Lions -2.5 ( via DraftKings ) Lions vs. Patriots prediction I think the Patriots will make some adjustments from last week and come out stronger in Week 10. This game could really go either way and we will know if the Patriots offense has the juice to win right away, as their first few drives tend to establish the rest of the game. If New England's defense can bounce back and Maye can stop giving the ball away, they can keep themselves in the playoff conversation with a win. Since it's an early kickoff, it's best to get your bets in sooner rather than later, because if you don't have your morning coffee, you could end up placing the wrong bet! Last week was a losing week, as the Lions' defense did their part, but the offense struggled more than I expected. Now two games below .500, we need a perfect 3/3 week to get back above, or at least two out of the three to get back to even. Here are three wagers to watch in this matchup. The odds are with FanDuel Sportsbook . 1. Jared Goff Over 268.5 passing yards (-112) Lions quarterback Jared Goff is having a solid season so far, and despite a quiet game against the Miami Dolphins last week, I think he will rebound well against New England. Green Bay Packers quarterback Jordan Love just threw for 372 yards against the Patriots, the most they've allowed this season. That was at home for New England too; now they are on the road and without their top cornerback, Carlton Davis III. Goff will want to rebound after being held without a passing touchdown for the first time this season last week. With his star wide receiver, Amon-Ra St. Brown, also having ties to Germany, he will do his best to get him a touchdown in front of his home crowd. Goff has thrown for over 268 yards in five games this season, and with New England allowing an average of 231.9 yards per game, going above that by only 37 seems doable with the weapons he has. Bet potential winnings: $10 -> $18.85 2. Jameson Williams Alt receiving yards 50+ (-158) Piggybacking off the first point with Goff, I think this secondary, without its No. 2 corner Davis, will have its hands full with wide receivers St. Brown and Jameson Williams. The Packers' top two receivers got over 100 yards each in last week's win, and each also had at least one catch over 40 yards. Williams is a big-play receiver; he can do that on one play, too. His speed will be tough to contain, and even on short to intermediate routes, he can turn a three-yard catch or a 10-yard snag into something more. St. Brown will probably receive the most attention, which gives Williams a chance to break out and take advantage of the lackluster secondary. Williams has only gotten this line in three games this season, and he could've had it last week if he didn't drop a catch. Where Goff can find Williams is in play-action. Goff can have the offense believe it's a run and suddenly, Williams is downfield wide open. When it comes to play action, New England is in for a world of trouble. Bet potential winnings: $10 -> $16.33 3. Amon-Ra St. Brown anytime touchdown (-130) As I mentioned earlier, St. Brown has German ties and will want to show out for the "home" crowd. When reporters asked him Friday if he already had a touchdown celebration in mind because of the circumstances, he said: "I don't have it planned yet, I still have two days to figure that out. You know, I haven't been in the endzone in some weeks so I feel like Germany would be a great time to touch the paint again." St. Brown is in a bit of a rut when it comes to finding the end zone, as he hasn't scored since Week 3. Five straight games without a touchdown is the longest he's gone without one since the end of the 2022 season, when he didn't score in the last five games. He also had seven straight games without a touchdown that season. This bet is strictly vibes-based and can sometimes be a bust, but I think the stars are aligning too much for you not to think the Lions and Goff won't have plays drawn up for him to score. Gibbs is averaging four catches a game, and he was held to none against Miami and only two against the Minnesota Vikings. I think he gets back on track this week with at least four. Speaking of the receiving game, St. Brown won't just find the end zone on Sunday; I think he will be a go-to option for Goff, which won't be surprising. St. Brown is averaging 7.6 catches a game this season, so I think he can hit eight. St. Brown will want to put on as much of a show as he can in Germany, so he seems like the best guy to lean on this week. The worst fears of the New England Patriots might have been realized after quarterback Drake Maye suffered an ankle injury while playing the Detroit Lions on Sunday, November 15. Maye, 24, will miss "an extended period, and possibly the remainder of the season," ESPN reported on Monday, November 16. The quarterback left the game, which took place in Munich, Germany, during the first quarter after he was sacked by Lions defensive end Aidan Hutchinson . Hutchinson, 26, also suffered a knee injury on the play after celebrating the sack. There is fear Hutchinson tore his ACL and will miss the remainder of the season. Patriots head coach Mike Vrabel explained that Maye did not immediately head home with the team. Clip of Sam Hartman Flirting With Fan's Mom Resurfaces After ‘Bachelor' News Vrabel added, "Just wanted to make sure everything was in line for him to travel - and it seems like he is. He'll be returning here, I think, shortly." Immediately after the game, Vrabel told reporters that Maye would "get more tests run" when he returned stateside. "He couldn't function, couldn't play, couldn't do whatever he needed to do to play quarterback, to protect himself, to execute or function at that level," Vrabel explained. Vrabel downplayed any malicious intent on Hutchinson's behalf, telling reporters, "I don't think it was anything intentional." Taylor Swift Seemingly Skips Chiefs-Falcons Game After CMA Awards Announcement "I'm sure that it wasn't," Vrabel added. "That's part of the game." Backup quarterback Tommy DeVito stepped in and played the rest of the game for the Patriots. The Lions dominated New England in Maye's absence, winning 35-10. "I'm going to continue the process I have been doing up to this point," DeVito said after Sunday's game. "Something that as a [backup], as cliche as it sounds, you have to be prepared to be a starter. So just keep doing what I'm doing, keep my head down, and then if something like that were to happen, you would have the reps and practice and the walkthroughs and everything going forward, so just keep on preparing and on to the next."

away.headline: A big Munich test for Lions and Patriots as injuries loom for New England
away.blurb: Injuries are a top concern for New England. Before traveling Wednesday night, the Patriots ruled out LG Ben Brown (knee), CB Carlton Davis III (knee) and RB TreVeyon Henderson (illness). November 12, 2026 / 5:07 PM EST / AP Heading into international games, NFL coaches typically talk up the niceties of "growing the game" globally. The New England Patriots (5-4) have lost two of their past three games and have a slew of injury concerns, including running back Rhamondre Stevenson. The Detroit Lions, even with a 6-2 record and four straight victories, are trying to keep pace in the tight NFC North. Sunday's game in Munich is a big one for both teams. Lions coach Dan Campbell wasn't focused on the international implications. "Well, if I'm being honest, I just haven't thought that far into it. I'm like, 'We've got to get prepared,'" Campbell said. The Patriots were embarrassed at home by the Green Bay Packers last week, losing 45-27, with Drake Maye throwing three interceptions and the secondary struggling to contain the Packers' passing game. Campbell expects a much-improved New England team on Sunday. "You look at the totality of what this team is capable of, the firepower they have, and they're a good team. They're dangerous," he said. "And they're going to clean a lot of things up." The Lions slogged through a 19-9 win over the rebuilding Miami Dolphins last week, relying on four field goals from Jake Bates. It was also just one week after a neck injury to All-Pro linebacker Jack Campbell. Detroit's bye week is in the rearview mirror, and after Munich, the team will host Tampa Bay and then Chicago on Thanksgiving Day. "It's a good thing to be tested during the season," Campbell said. "It really is. And to have to go through some of these tough stretches because that's what the playoffs are. That's what it is. And certainly if you got to go on the road. So, that's what this is. This is about us. This is the next obstacle we have. Told the team we're not going to clear it. Our objective is to go through it, and that's the mindset." Stevenson, the team's leading rusher with 399 yards on 102 carries, didn't practice Wednesday because of a knee injury. That could put second-year running back Corey Kiner in line for the bulk of the carries. "Corey has done a really nice job, but there are also some things that Corey has to be able to improve on," coach Mike Vrabel said, citing "recognition of the pressure and then the ability to block the pressure." The coach said "a lot of contending teams" are 5-4. "We've got to start putting ourselves in position to play meaningful games in January or in the middle of January," Vrabel said. "It's usually what happens in the National Football League; a bunch of teams get bunched up, and they go in different directions, and I know the direction that we're going to head in, and that's going to be the one that's forward, positive and winning." home.headline: Aidan Hutchinson injury update has Lions DE with torn ACL: Live updates
home.blurb: He is going to be out for the rest of the 2026 season with an ACL tear in his right knee , according to reports from two top NFL newsbreakers Monday morning. A few hours after the Lions won 35-10 for their fifth straight victory, reports came out that the team was "bracing for bad news" with the likelihood Hutchinson misses the rest of the season for the second time in three years. Hutchinson broke bones in his left leg in 2024 against Dallas on a sack. He made the Pro Bowl last season in his return to the field, recording a career-high 14½ sacks while playing all 17 games, and signed a mammoth new contract extension in October 2025 that begins in 2027. Aidan Hutchinson ACL tear has him out for season: Reports The Ringer's Tom Pelissero on Sunday afternoon was first to definitively report Hutchinson would be out for the season, but the injury was unclear. Now, we await an official announcement from the Lions, who arrived back in Michigan overnight. They are off Monday, ahead of this Sunday's home game against Tampa Bay (3-6) . Report: Aidan Hutchinson out for season He eventually walked off with medical personnel, underwent a lengthy evaluation in the blue medical tent on the Lions sideline and then walked to the locker room. He was ruled questionable initially and then ruled out in the third quarter. He reportedly then underwent an MRI and German media outlet Joyn posted a picture of Hutchinson on crutches outside of the Lions’ team bus. Aidan Hutchinson will be 'out for the season' Reporters started putting out information just before 2 p.m. ET that the Lions fear Hutchinson will be out for the season after a significant knee injury. The Ringer's Tom Pelissero had the strongest wording, saying, "Imaging in Munich confirmed the injury to Hutchinson, whose right knee buckled as he celebrated a sack against the Patriots. He’s out for the season." The Lions recorded four sacks of Patriots backup QB Tommy DeVito after Hutchinson's injury. (Drake Maye hurt his ankle on Hutchinson's sack and also did not return.) Hutchinson hurt his knee Sunday celebrating a first-quarter sack against the New England Patriots in Munich, Germany. Hutchinson is the second Lions defensive captain to experience a significant injury in the past two weeks, after middle linebacker Jack Campbell suffered a spinal injury Nov. 1 and remains in a Detroit area hospital. Here are the latest updates and news on the Hutchinson situation: Ian Rapoport of ESPN/NFL Network (and ESPN's Adam Schefter) confirmed on Monday morning the worst fears: Initial tests in Munich showed Hutchinson suffered a torn ACL in his right knee. Hutchinson also "likely suffered additional damage in the knee, with concern about his meniscus, sources told Rapoport." Larry Lage of the Associated Press on Sunday evening is the latest to report that, as feared, Hutchinson will miss the rest of the season . home.headline: A big Munich test for Lions and Patriots as injuries loom for New England
home.blurb: Injuries are a top concern for New England. Before traveling Wednesday night, the Patriots ruled out LG Ben Brown (knee), CB Carlton Davis III (knee) and RB TreVeyon Henderson (illness). November 12, 2026 / 5:07 PM EST / AP Heading into international games, NFL coaches typically talk up the niceties of "growing the game" globally. The New England Patriots (5-4) have lost two of their past three games and have a slew of injury concerns, including running back Rhamondre Stevenson. The Detroit Lions, even with a 6-2 record and four straight victories, are trying to keep pace in the tight NFC North. Sunday's game in Munich is a big one for both teams. Lions coach Dan Campbell wasn't focused on the international implications. "Well, if I'm being honest, I just haven't thought that far into it. I'm like, 'We've got to get prepared,'" Campbell said. The Patriots were embarrassed at home by the Green Bay Packers last week, losing 45-27, with Drake Maye throwing three interceptions and the secondary struggling to contain the Packers' passing game. Campbell expects a much-improved New England team on Sunday. "You look at the totality of what this team is capable of, the firepower they have, and they're a good team. They're dangerous," he said. "And they're going to clean a lot of things up." The Lions slogged through a 19-9 win over the rebuilding Miami Dolphins last week, relying on four field goals from Jake Bates. It was also just one week after a neck injury to All-Pro linebacker Jack Campbell. Detroit's bye week is in the rearview mirror, and after Munich, the team will host Tampa Bay and then Chicago on Thanksgiving Day. "It's a good thing to be tested during the season," Campbell said. "It really is. And to have to go through some of these tough stretches because that's what the playoffs are. That's what it is. And certainly if you got to go on the road. So, that's what this is. This is about us. This is the next obstacle we have. Told the team we're not going to clear it. Our objective is to go through it, and that's the mindset." Stevenson, the team's leading rusher with 399 yards on 102 carries, didn't practice Wednesday because of a knee injury. That could put second-year running back Corey Kiner in line for the bulk of the carries. "Corey has done a really nice job, but there are also some things that Corey has to be able to improve on," coach Mike Vrabel said, citing "recognition of the pressure and then the ability to block the pressure." The coach said "a lot of contending teams" are 5-4. "We've got to start putting ourselves in position to play meaningful games in January or in the middle of January," Vrabel said. "It's usually what happens in the National Football League; a bunch of teams get bunched up, and they go in different directions, and I know the direction that we're going to head in, and that's going to be the one that's forward, positive and winning." picks.blurb: FalconsSI Staff Unanimous in Falcons vs. Chiefs Predictions Skip to main content SI.COM Betting Sites Sportsbook Promos BetMGM Bonus Code Fanatics Sportsbook Promo Canada Sportsbook Promos bet365 CA Bonus Code Rainbet Promo Code Stake Promo Code PREDICTION MARKETS College Market Prediction Market Apps Prediction Market Promos Kalshi Promo Code Kalshi Referral Code Apps like Kalshi Polymarket Promo Code Polymarket Referral Code Novig Promo Code Underdog Promo Code Stadium Wonders Digital Covers Push Notifications Digital Subscription Customer Service Prospects by SI The Atlanta Falcons are looking to get back on track in Week 10, but they face a difficult challenge with Patrick Mahomes and the Kansas City Chiefs coming to Mercedes-Benz Stadium. Atlanta has lost four of its last five games and is coming off a disappointing performance against the Cincinnati Bengals in Madrid. Now, the Falcons will have to find a way to slow down another talented quarterback while dealing with significant changes to their own roster. Kansas City will enter the matchup without running back Kenneth Walker III , which could make things more manageable for Atlanta’s struggling defense. However, Mahomes and Travis Kelce remain major threats, and the Chiefs have plenty of weapons to exploit the Falcons’ defensive weaknesses and deficiencies. How will the game play out? The FalconsSI staff delivers its weekly predictions. Scott Kennedy (4-5) The Falcons have had some frustrating games this year, suffering through two weeks of Cooper Rush and a monsoon in Tampa, for example. But last week in Madrid was different. The Cincinnati Bengals simply showed the Falcons aren't good enough this year. Their defense has been patched together with duct tape and one-year contracts, and it simply couldn't hold up against Joe Burrow, Ja'Marr Chase, and Tee Higgins. General manager Ian Cunningham saw the same thing we did, and rather than deluding himself into thinking 3-6 in a weak NFC South was good enough, he sold at the trade deadline. Now Patrick Mahomes and Travis Kelce come to Mercedes-Benz Stadium, and the Falcons are without All-Pro safety Jessie Bates III after trading him to the Jaguars. Mahomes and the Chiefs aren't as explosive as the Bengals, but, well, they're still Mahomes and the Chiefs... and they're better on defense. We'll see if Michael Penix Jr. and the offense can play well enough to take another step towards feeling good about Penix in 2027, but the Falcons are staring 3-7 in the face. Prediction: Chiefs 31, Falcons 17 Gerald Thomas, III (4-5) The notion of the Falcons playing up to the competition is fading away. Plus, there’s a belief that Atlanta is now playing for draft positioning instead of ending its playoff drought. The Chiefs present too many issues for the Falcons. We all know what Patrick Mahomes can do in the passing attack. And we all watched the Atlanta secondary struggle with Bengals playmakers in Madrid. With Kenneth Walker III out, that may soften the blow against the Falcons’ dwindling run defense . Offensively, Atlanta is looking pretty “eh.” Michael Penix Jr. has gotten off of his heater and must prove himself as the franchise quarterback against one of the top pass defenses in the league. Additionally, Kansas City is top-10 at stopping the run and will likely stack boxes to stonewall Bijan Robinson as the Falcons deal with the key loss of powerback Brian Robinson Jr. Atlanta is looking at a third consecutive loss on the road to the 2027 NFL Draft. Prediction: Chiefs 34, Falcons 21 Garrett Chapman (4-5) The Falcons have lost four of their last five, and the road to snapping that skid will run through the Kansas City Chiefs. The perennial contenders will be without Kenneth Walker, but Patrick Mahomes and Travis Kelce are still willing and able to run wild on a reeling Falcons defense that just moved Jessie Bates. On offense, Corey Levin will be taking over at center , and he'll have a pretty difficult challenge opposite him. This should be a tight game, but I'm not sure the Falcons can overcome this team opposite them right now. Prediction: Chiefs 20, Falcons 17 Darius Hayes (4-5) Expects a closer game with Walker sidelined, but Mahomes will ultimately make the difference. Atlanta’s defense has continued to struggle, and the departure of Bates doesn’t provide much confidence that things will improve against Kansas City’s passing attack. The Falcons also face questions offensively with a new starting center stepping into the lineup midway through the season. That transition could create additional problems against a talented Chiefs defense. Atlanta remains competitive, but Kansas City will pull away late to secure the victory. Prediction: Chiefs 23, Falcons 16 Jerry Jones, Falcons Podcast , (4-5) Despite being only a half game back from first place in the division, it really seems like the clock is ticking on the Falcons’ season. The performances in recent weeks and the trades the Falcons made at the deadline make this game feel like a “crap or get off the pot” moment for this team. There is hope, though. The Chiefs are good, but the Falcons have beaten better teams this year (which sounds crazy given they’ve only won three games). The blueprint for beating the Chiefs is pretty straightforward: stop the run. The issue is, the Falcons have struggled to do that, especially against inside runs, and the Chiefs are an inside-running team. If they can pull it off, the Falcons’ pass defense matches up well against the Chiefs’ passing offense on paper (even without Jessie Bates). On the other side of the ball, the Chiefs’ defense has been solid, but I think they have a real weakness in the secondary with the injury to their rookie Mansoor Delane. To exploit it, though, the Falcons will need to get the run game going. Their passing offense has been pretty ineffective when the ground game stalls. This is a game the Falcons can win... but whether they will is a different story. Prediction: Chiefs 24, Falcons 16 Final Predictions: Chiefs Are the Unanimous Pick Despite differences in the projected final scores, all five contributors are picking Kansas City to win in Week 10. The absence of Kenneth Walker could give Atlanta an opportunity to make this a more competitive matchup, but Mahomes remains the biggest difference-maker heading into Sunday. For the Falcons, the challenge will be finding a way to slow down Kansas City’s passing attack while getting enough production from Penix and the offense. Atlanta needs a win to stop its recent slide, but the consensus among our staff is that the Chiefs will leave Mercedes-Benz Stadium with another victory. Kickoff is set for 1:00 p.m. EST at Mercedes-Benz Stadium and will be shown on CBS. It's been mostly positive on the results front for the Kansas City Chiefs, who come into Sunday's game against the Atlanta Falcons sitting at a healthy 6-2 overall. Although Atlanta seems to be trending in the wrong direction, it's still in business to compete in a lackluster NFC South. Could that lead to an inspired home performance against visiting Kansas City, or will it be smooth sailing for head coach Andy Reid's group? With kickoff on the horizon, which side will come out on top today? The Kansas City Chiefs On SI crew makes its predictions for Week 10 of the regular season. Joshua Brisco: The loss of Kenneth Walker impacts how the Chiefs may choose to manage this game, but it shouldn’t change the final result. Kansas City still has the advantage on both sides of the ball, even though Atlanta has punched above its weight twice this season. Ultimately, I expect the Chiefs to navigate through a relatively tough game and return home with the win. Jordan Foote: Being down Walker undoubtedly could make life more difficult for the Chiefs, but rookie Emmett Johnson's been nothing short of awesome when on the field. Look for him to leave attempts at tackles behind on Sunday afternoon and factor into a passing game that has a less-than-100% Xavier Worthy but a new addition in Josh Downs. The real intrigue, in my view, comes on the defensive side. Can Steve Spagnuolo's unit find a way to slow down running back Bijan Robinson and wideout Drake London? If so, putting the fate of the game in quarterback Michael Penix Jr.'s hands seems like a losing formula for Atlanta. It may not be as pretty and resounding as Week 9's throttling of the Jets was, but it should be another victory regardless. Joshua Schulman: Coming off a much-needed bounce-back win at home, the Chiefs will hit the road against a perplexing Falcons squad. They have defeated the 49ers at home and put up 45 points on their division rival Saints on the road, yet they were also shut out by the Buccaneers in a four-interception outing from Michael Penix Jr. Ultimately, I think this will come down to the version of Atlanta that shows up. The Falcons rank in the bottom half of the league in both rushing and passing defense, so I’m expecting Emmett Johnson to wreak havoc on the ground despite Kenneth Walker’s absence. It’ll also be Josh Downs’ first appearance in the red and gold after he was acquired via trade from the Colts. I do think the threat of Bijan Robinson and being away from home will keep this close, but I have Kansas City pulling away in a narrow finish. Tyler Brown: Nothing like a Week 9 win against the Jets to trick the mind into thinking Kansas City turned the corner after an explosive second half, but that might be what happened. Setting aside the Harrison Butker and Josh Simmons drama, the Chiefs looked like an inspired team led by their old faithful stars. Travis Kelce and Chris Jones both posted big performances, and Rashee Rice and George Karlaftis are becoming key cogs in their respective units. A mid-season acquisition like Josh Downs can also provide a shot in the arm for a team. This game will be won in the trenches. Atlanta has Robinson, the NFL’s leading rusher, so the Chiefs’ defensive line and linebackers will need a big day to contain him. If they do, Penix, the worst quarterback in the league when facing pressure, will be forced to beat them. On the other side, Walker’s injury leaves the Chiefs’ rushing attack in question. With Kahlil Benson and Josh Ezeudu starting at tackle, the Chiefs will need a big day from Johnson. I think they get it done, kicking the Falcons while they’re down in the same week they traded away their best center and safety. Don’t get me wrong, Atlanta has a lot to play for, just a half-game back in a weak NFC South despite being 3-6. They are getting further and further away from their wins over the 6-3 Packers and 7-1 49ers, however. Published Nov 15, 2026 JORDAN FOOTE Jordan Foote covers the Kansas City Chiefs for Chiefs On SI. Cox/Getty Images) | Getty Images Jared Sapp · SB Nation Fri, November 13, 2026 at 9:30 PM UTC · 9 min read Advertisement Advertisement About Our Ads College Sports Sports Business Women's Sports College & High School Adventure Sports What & How To Watch Responsible Gaming Share Your Feedback About Our Ads It's time for the Arrowhead Pride staff to put their opinions to the test. Before the Kansas City Chiefs travel to face the Atlanta Falcons , our writers predicted the final score and result. Atlanta has been an unpredictable team both looking dominant in their trio of wins while struggling in most of their six losses. FanDuel Sportsbook currently lists the Chiefs as 3.5-point home favorites. The Falcons also have the misfortune of not coming off of a European game into their bye week. The Falcons lost 34-17 to the Cincinnati Bengals in Madrid, Spain on Sunday. They also sent starting safety Jessie Bates to the Jacksonville Jaguars ahead of Tuesday's trade deadline. We also want to know your score prediction! Vote in the poll on The Feed and share your score prediction ! Jared Sapp ( @TrumanChief ) I do worry about the Falcons' pass rush, even if their defense's other two levels were underwhelming even before trading Bates. With the league's two best running backs facing off, I expect a run heavy day that should lead to a fast moving game. Look for the Chiefs' pass rush to build on their second half against Atlanta quarterback Michael Penix. This will be a game where Atlanta looks game for a couple of drives before the Chiefs overwhelm in route to a victory. The run game will lead to limited possessions for both sides to keep the scoring from getting out of hand. Chiefs 27, Falcons 17 Caleb James ( @CJScoobs ) The Chiefs and Falcons are on opposite ends of the competitive spectrum in the NFL, and this week's game should show that. The Falcons traded away veteran safety Jessie Bates to the contending Jacksonville Jaguars, while the Chiefs traded for wide receiver Josh Downs from the Indianapolis Colts. Despite a talented core of offensive playmakers, including Bijan Robinson and Drake London, the Falcons are only 3-6, largely because their defense allows over 340 yards per game. The Falcons are -8 in the turnover-takeaway category, 30th in the NFL, while the Chiefs are tied for 9th at +4. If they can force turnovers, they will be in good shape to win the game. I don't think Downs will play more than 20 snaps this week, but I would expect the Chiefs to design a few routes for him to get his feet wet in the offense. Chiefs 27, Falcons 13 Mark Gunnels ( @MarkAGunnels ) I've got the Chiefs winning this one. Josh Downs makes his debut, and I like Mahomes having another guy who can get open underneath, especially now that Atlanta traded away Jessie Bates. The Falcons also traded their starting center, Ryan Neuzil, so I expect Chris Jones to make life real uncomfortable up the middle. Chiefs 27, Falcons 20 Maurice Elston ( @MrMauriceElston ) What impressed me most about the Chiefs' 35–12 win over the Jets was how they finished. Kansas City has a habit of letting teams it should beat hang around, and the Jets were within two points at halftime. The Chiefs outscored them 21–0 from there. Kenneth Walker III looked like the player we saw during the 5–0 start, finishing with 143 yards from scrimmage and three touchdowns. To keep Walker rolling, the Chiefs need their receivers to win against man coverage. Seattle and Denver showed what happens when defenses can load the box and trust their corners to hold up one-on-one: the run slows down, and play-action loses its bite. If the receivers make Atlanta pay for that approach, Walker will have more room to run and Patrick Mahomes can get back to attacking off play-action. Against Atlanta, the key is slowing down Bijan Robinson. That's the operative phrase: slow him down. He's coming off 100 rushing yards and another 47 through the air, so Kansas City has to account for him even when he doesn't get the handoff. Drake London demands attention, and Kyle Pitts can still cause problems for the Chiefs' linebackers and safeties even in a quiet season. But if Kansas City's run defense keeps Robinson from taking over, Sack Nation can build on its five-sack performance by moving Michael Penix Jr. off his spot and forcing him past his first read. I like the Chiefs' chances when Atlanta has to win that way. Matt Stagner ( @stagdsp ) Your Kansas City Chiefs head to Atlanta as big favorites against the 2-6 Falcons. Yes, they've lost 4 of their last 5, but this is a dangerous opponent. They've got the league's best RB and a streaky young QB– it's an offense that can get out to an early lead and make things uncomfortable. But, as always, this game will come down to how the Chiefs execute. From the pass protection to the receivers and the short-yardage offense, this team has questions, but they're more than capable. Ideally, they start strong with Walker and Johnson– if the run game gets going, the Chiefs are hard to beat. Chiefs 33, Falcons 21 Dakota Watson ( @D_Watson56 ) The Chiefs enter this game after righting some of their wrongs last week against the Jets, although still with major question marks for a team intent on making a Super Bowl run. The Falcons, meanwhile, are on a two game losing skid after their upset win over the previously unbeaten San Francisco 49ers. I never quite know what to make of the Falcons. They're a team with some of the best offensive weapons in the entire NFL, yet they can't ever seem to put it all together. Since Jonathan Taylor in week 2, Bijan Robinson will be the best running back the Chiefs have faced all season. The Chiefs have been great defending the run in 2026, and I think they will be able to contain Robinson, but he will still get his yards. Defensively, the Chiefs should also be able to continue the positive momentum they established last week in pressuring the quarterback and leading to mistakes by the Falcons' offense. I'm excited to see what the Chiefs' offense has in store for new wide receiver Josh Downs. I'm keeping my expectations in check, however, as it always seems like the Chiefs onboard their wide receivers slowly. I expect Downs to play 35-50% of the team's snaps, but they will still be able to generate enough offense to take home the win. Rocky Magana ( @RockyMagana ) The Atlanta Falcons only show up for primetime games; they are garbage during noon kickoffs. Despite having multiple weapons on offense, namely running back Bijan Robinson and wide receiver Drake London, they can never seem to put it all together in the daytime. On the other hand, the Chiefs are coming off one of their best performances of the season, when the pass rush finally woke up and bullied a terrible team in the New York Jets. At the end of the day, I would expect the Chiefs offense to continue rolling while they ramp up new acquisition wide receiver Josh Downs. Chiefs 31, Atlanta 17 Nate Christensen Atlanta has been a surprisingly competitive team since quarterback Michael Penix Jr. came back. The Falcons have one of the dynamic duos of weapons in running back Bijan Robinson and Drake London. That alongside a decent offensive line has given the Falcons a shot to win any game. Their defense has been surprisingly competent, but after trading Jessie Bates, that will probably fall off. I expect Atlanta to have some nice drives against the Chiefs, but the game will play out similarly to the Jets game. At some point, the Chiefs pressure will get to a pocket-bound Penix and Atlanta won't be able to catch up offensively. Chiefs pull away in the second half. Chiefs 28, Falcons 17 Ron Kopp Jr. ( @RonOnChiefs ) If the Falcons hadn't traded away two starters this week, this would feel much more like a spot where the Chiefs could slip up. Still, noon kickoffs have seemed to come with slow starts for Kansas City this year, and this Falcons team still has a reason to fight to stay tied for first place in the NFC South. However, Atlanta has had more letdowns than triumphs this year, including a couple of weeks ago when the Tampa Bay Buccaneers ran for 342 yards as a team and didn't need a pass to win. This game should be a comfortable win for Kansas City because of its offense, leaning on the ground game once again to stay in rhtyhm and open up the middle of the field for passes. 2026 Standings Nate Chrstensen Maurice Elston Dakota Watson All nine panelists predicted the Chiefs to win by more than ten points. Ron (38-20) and Matt (28-13) had the most accurate Week 9 predictions with only 16 total points of error. Our readers were less optimistic about how Kansas City would perform. Only 50.6% of our readers anticipated a comfortable Chiefs victory, while 37.2% expected Mahomes and Company to narrowly come out on top. 12.2% of respondents expected the Jets to win. *To calculate a prediction's points of error, the differences between the prediction and the actual score in point spread, home team score, and away team score are added together. For example, a prediction calls for a 17-10 Chiefs win. They end up winning 16-10, so there were two points of error: the point spread was off by one point, the Kansas City score missed by one point, and the opponent's score was predicted correctly. But if the Chiefs lose the game 17-10, there were 28 points of error in the prediction: the point spread was off by 14 (the difference between +7 and -7), and both scores were off by 7.

(Photo by Justin Edmonds/Getty Images) Getty Nick Roesch · HEAVY Fri, November 13, 2026 at 11:51 PM UTC · 3 min read Advertisement Advertisement About Our Ads College Sports Sports Business Women's Sports College & High School Adventure Sports What & How To Watch Responsible Gaming Share Your Feedback About Our Ads The Kansas City Chiefs wrapped their final practice of the week on Friday ahead on their road matchup against the Atlanta Falcons in Week 10. Kansas City is dealing with a few key injuries that could impact Sunday's game. The headliner is running back Kenneth Walker III, who is questionable to play after sustaining a groin injury. Of course, when injuries occur, it provides an opportunity for someone else to step up. Joshua Ezeudu Will Start in Place of Jaylon Moore for Kansas City Chiefs vs. Falcons Starting right tackle Jaylon Moore sustained an ankle injury during last week's win over the New York Jets . He has been ruled out against Atlanta after not participating in any practices this week. Getting the start in his place will be Joshua Ezeudu, who the Chiefs acquired in a trade with the New York Giants back in August. Ezeudu was a third-round draft pick by the Giants in 2022. He appeared in 16 games for New York during his four-year tenure, starting 10. A calf injury cost him the entire 2025 season. Ezeudu started for Moore in Week 7 against the Seattle Seahawks . While speaking to the media on Friday, coach Andy Reid gave Ezeudu a big vote of confidence. "We feel comfortable with him in there," Reid said. "He did a nice job for us last week, and the other times that he's had to fill in." Chiefs' Final Week 10 Injury Report Here is the final injury report for Kansas City's matchup against the Falcons: RT Jaylon Moore- Out (Ankle) DT Peter Woods- Out (Neck) DT Omarr Norman-Lott- Out (Knee) RB Kenneth Walker III- Questionable (Groin) RB Jayden Ott- Questionable (Hamstring) CB Mansoor Delane- Questionable (Shoulder) WR Xavier Worthy- No Designation (Hamstring) QB Justin Fields- No Designation (Neck) LB Jeffrey Bassa- No Designation (Hand) S Jaden Hicks- No Designation (Shoulder) TE Travis Kelce- No Designation (Ankle) QB Patrick Mahomes- No Designation (Knee, Elbow) WR Rashee Rice- No Designation (Knee) Like Moore, Woods also missed the entire week of practice. He injured his neck back in Week 8 against the Denver Broncos , which Reid has called a "stinger." Delane has also missed the last two games with a shoulder injury that has plagued him since OTAs. Worthy made rapid progress after hurting his hamstring against the Jets last week and is good to go against Atlanta. The same can be said for Mahomes' elbow injury, which gave the Chiefs a scare last week. Norman-Lott continues to ramp up toward making his season debut, possibly as soon as next week. Home-field advantage has diminished circuit-wide, and Atlanta’s 1-4 record is a prime example. The Chiefs defense is third in scoring and sixth in yards per rush, so it can put this game in Penix's hands on defense and Kenneth Walker's hands on offense in order to get a lead and keep it. My ratings say this line should be Chiefs -6 and I was hoping the market would give us a -3 at some point.

away.headline: Chiefs battled through more injury problems in victory over Atlanta Falcons
away.blurb: “I thought guys that stepped in really helped us out,” Chiefs coach Andy Reid said. Johnson demonstrated his readiness for more work based on his performance in Denver two weeks ago, when he accounted for 143 combined yards plus a 44-yard kickoff return. Walker’s status for the next game, Sunday at home against the Arizona Cardinals, won’t be known until later this week. Reid announced the injury on Friday and didn’t rule Walker out until the next day. Chiefs beat the Falcons 35-13 despite injuries across the offense. Emmett Johnson posted 101 rushing yards, 70 receiving yards and two scores. Jared Wiley fractured an ankle, and Trey Smith entered concussion protocol. The Chiefs went to Atlanta for Sunday’s showdown against the Falcons without their leading rusher and starting right tackle. During the game, they lost their right guard and backup tight end. Meanwhile, star tight end Travis Kelce hobbled off the field and center starting Creed Humphrey left the game after getting his eye poked. The Chiefs survived it all, even thrived, in defeating the Atlanta Falcons 35-13 partly because the replacements didn’t miss a beat. Rookie running back Emmett Johnson made the biggest splash. He got his first NFL start in place of Kenneth Walker, who showed up on the injury report late in the week with a strained groin. Against the Falcons he was even better, leading the Chiefs in both rushing — 101 yards — and receiving. He had six receptions for 70 yards and two touchdowns. Chiefs tight end Jared Wiley suffered the most serious injury, fracturing an ankle. That happened in the first quarter. Kelce’s injury occurred when he was tackled after a 23-yard reception. Reid said Kelce, who has been dealing with ankle problems this year, injured his calf. He re-entered the game in the second quarter. “He got twisted up a little bit,” Reid said. The tight end position continued to produce in spite of the injuries, with Jake Briningstool hauling in a 20-yard catch, the longest of his nine-game NFL career. Also in the first quarter, guard Trey Smith left the game and Reid said he has entered the concussion protocol. Mike Caliendo, who had played left guard instead of Kingsley Suamataia in two games this season, filled in for Smith. Elsewhere on the offensive line, center Creed Humphrey took a finger in the face and left the game. Television replays showed a cut under his eye. Mike Nourzad got some snaps before Humphrey returned. Besides Walker, the Chiefs entered the game without right tackle Jaylon Moore, who missed the start with an ankle injury. Josh Ezeudu made his second start of the season. It appeared rookie cornerback Mansoor Delane, who has missed time with a shoulder injury, may have re-injured himself. But Reid said he should be OK. “He landed on his back, near that shoulder area,” Reid said. “I think he scared him more than anything. He’s going to be all right.” This story was originally published November 15, 2026 at 5:19 PM . Chiefs’ report card reflects

away.blurb: Per ESPN's Adam Schefter , the Chiefs are going to hold Walker out of Sunday's game against the Atlanta Falcons due to a groin injury because they "want to give him a week" rather than try to force him to play through it. For more from Bleacher Report, check out our B/R app , homepage and social feeds—including Twitter , Instagram , Facebook , TikTok and YouTube . After being a late addition to the injury report on Friday, Kansas City Chiefs running back Kenneth Walker III won't play in Week 10. NFL Network's Ian Rapoport added the injury is considered "minor" and the Chiefs want to exercise caution with Walker. From a fantasy perspective, Emmett Johnson should be a late addition to your roster on the waiver wire as he gets set to make his first career start. He is only rostered in 33 percent of leagues right now, per FantasyPros . Johnson was arguably the best player on the field for the Chiefs two weeks ago in their 28-24 loss to the Denver Broncos. He had 128 receiving yards and one touchdown on five receptions, as well as one carry for 15 yards in just 13 offensive snaps. Even though Atlanta's defense has been strong against the run, ranking third in EPA per rush, the ability Johnson showed as a receiver significantly boosts his fantasy value. away.headline: Chiefs Might Not Be Done Adding to Roster After Latest NFL News
away.blurb: After a two-year stint with the Chiefs, Brown signed a one-year, $6.5 million contract with Philadelphia during the offseason. He has recorded just five receptions for 63 yards in 2026, as an ankle injury has limited him to just four games played. The Kansas City Chiefs got promising early returns on new wide receiver Josh Downs during their Week 10 victory over the Atlanta Falcons. Downs caught four passes for 53 yards and one touchdown in his Chiefs debut. He will become a bigger force each week as he becomes more comfortable in the offense and gets the playbook down. The NFL trade deadline has passed, but there are still several free agents that can be signed, including one that Kansas City knows well. Former Kansas City Chiefs WR Marquise ‘Hollywood’ Brown Clears Waivers The Philadelphia Eagles waived wide receiver Hollywood Brown on Thursday. According to a report from NFL insider Mike Garafolo, Brown officially cleared waivers on Monday and is now free to sign with any team at any time. Brown signed with Kansas City in 2024. Unfortunately, he missed most of that season after sustaining a sternoclavicular injury on the first play of preseason. He returned in Week 16, and posted 14 catches for 141 yards in five games, including the playoffs. Brown bounced back nicely in 2025, leading all Chiefs wide receivers with 587 yards and tied for the team lead with five receiving touchdowns. He was a constant in the passing attack as Rashee Rice and Xavier Worthy missed several games. Do the Chiefs Have Room for Hollywood Brown? Kansas City’s receiver corps looked as good as it has all season against the Falcons. Downs, Cyrus Allen, and Andrew Armstrong each caught a touchdown pass and recorded at least 40 receiving yards. Rashee Rice also had a nice day with five receptions for 82 yards. The Chiefs could consider bringing Brown back due to the struggles of Xavier Worthy . It has been a disappointing year for Worthy, and he was held without a catch against Atlanta despite leading all receivers in snaps played with 56. Worthy has caught three or less passes in five games this season, and has not recorded more than 73 receiving yard in a single game. He also has just one touchdown catch, and simply hasn’t taken a step forward since his rookie season. If Kansas City bring Brown back, it would allow Worthy to take a step back and reset. He is only rostered in 33 percent of leagues right now, per FantasyPros . Johnson was arguably the best player on the field for the Chiefs two weeks ago in their 28-24 loss to the Denver Broncos. He had 128 receiving yards and one touchdown on five receptions, as well as one carry for 15 yards in just 13 offensive snaps. Even though Atlanta's defense has been strong against the run, ranking third in EPA per rush, the ability Johnson showed as a receiver significantly boosts his fantasy value. And it's a game for the Texans that'll be extremely important to take advantage of. They'll be taking the road trying to climb one game closer to .500, face up against another AFC Wild Card contender, and will be trying to build upon the 44-point outing they saw last weekend against the LA Chargers. So what can we expect from the Texans in this game against the Browns? Will they rise to the occasion for a second straight win, or fall into similar pitfalls that they have in their five losses so far this season? Well, let's sort through a batch of three bold predictions for the Texans to take our chances at guessing how things will unravel in Cleveland on Sunday: 1. The Browns, while they haven't allowed 30 points to an opponent dating back to Week 1 against the Jacksonville Jaguars, have certainly gotten close a few times. And on top of that, they haven't really played a high-powered offense like the Texans many times this season. If the Texans can keep their momentum through the air and the offense can continue to limit the penalties setting them back as they did last weekend, 30 points is wildly possible for this team. So far this season, the Browns are 0-1 in games where they allow 30 points or more, and have yet to score 30 points a game themselves. This might be a simple recipe for Houston's success this weekend. 2. The Browns are 3-0 at home this year, but after having lost two straight games, they are being treated like an afterthought this week. As you can see in the national picks below, not a single person is picking the Browns at home. Here is what the national media is saying about the Week 10 game between the Browns and Texans: NFL.com (Various) Why Brooke picked the Texans: Even sitting at 3-5, the Texans appear to be full steam ahead toward a playoff berth with the way their offense is playing and defense is improving. C.J. Stroud has Nick Caley's unit absolutely humming now that most of his main targets are healthy. The real key to that success is Nico Collins. In the 257 snaps Collins has played this season, the Texans have averaged 8.2 yards per passing play, more than the 49ers' league-leading 7.9. He could be stalled when matched up against cornerback Denzel Ward, who's allowing 0.5 yards per coverage snap, fifth-fewest among cornerbacks (min. 150 coverage snaps). That duel is sure to be dogfight Sunday, but no matter, as I have faith in Stroud's other weapons (Tank Dell, Marvin Harrison Jr., Kayshon Boutte and Xavier Hutchinson) to get it done. Houston's lone offensive weakness matches up nicely against the Browns' permeable run defense. Getting Deshaun Watson back is a boost for Cleveland, but even with him, the Browns have struggled to put together a full game, instead relying on a few big plays each week from their young stars. An all-around performance is exactly what the Browns must have to beat the current version of DeMeco Ryans' team. Thus, Cleveland will fall short of improving to 4-0 at home for the first time since the 1963 campaign, when Jim Brown led the NFL in rushing and scrimmage yards in a 14-game season. CBS Sports (Pete Prisco) – Texans 21, Browns 20 This is a big game for both teams in terms of the playoff picture. The Texans looked dominant against the Chargers last week, but this is a second straight road game. It won't matter. Their defensive front will dominate whoever plays quarterback for the Browns. But the Cleveland defense will keep them in it. CBS Sports (John Breech) – Texans 24, Browns 16 Anyway, this genuinely does feel like a game that's going to boil down to Watson vs. the Texans. Watson has been sacked more times than any other QB in the NFL this year (33), and he'll be facing a defense that leads the NFL in sacks (29). That's a recipe for disaster. There have only been three games all season where a QB has been sacked at least eight times: Two of them were Deshaun Watson (vs. Jets in Week 5 and vs. Steelers in Week 8) and the other one happened on Sunday with the Texans sacking Justin Herbert eight times. Sporting News (Vinnie Iyer) – Texans 20, Browns 17 The Texans hope to sneak back into the playoff picture and their defense got back to making big plays in Los Angeles after the bye. Cleveland's defense will get a break as Houston is one-dimensional out of necessity, but in the end, old Texans friend Deshaun Watson will be outdueled by red-hot C.J. Stroud. Sporting News (Bill Bender) – Texans 22, Browns 19 Shedeur Sanders had 297 passing yards and two TDs in his first start of the season, and that might be enough to keep that in a home start against the Texans. Houston quarterback C.J. Stroud is coming off a 384-yard, five-TD performance against the Chargers. The Browns' early-season shine is wearing off, but they are 4-0 ATS as an underdog of seven points or less. Linebacker Carson Schwesinger, who has 25 tackles the last two weeks, helps Cleveland stick around at home. Below are our Week 10 NFL staff picks:

picks.blurb: Week 10 picks: Who the experts are taking in Texans vs. Browns - Yahoo Sports Search Query for Search Search Home News Finance Sports More Mail NFL Power Rankings Fantasy Football NFL Power Rankings Week 11 Waiver Wire Chargers get first win College football Top 25 Latest NFL updates Week 10 picks: Who the experts are taking in Texans vs. Browns Advertisement Advertisement About Our Ads College Sports Sports Business Women's Sports College & High School Adventure Sports What & How To Watch Responsible Gaming Share Your Feedback About Our Ads So, is this the week when the Houston Texans begin a new winning streak? Currently sitting at 3-5, the Texans must get back to their winning ways long-term if they plan on making a postseason push in the AFC. Right now, no one should be talking about the playoffs, especially since Houston has blown three fourth-quarter leads and remains winless at home. The good news? Sunday's matchup is on the road, a place where Houston is 3-1. The Texans will travel to Cleveland for a date with Deshaun Watson and the Browns in Week 10. Cleveland, which could be gunning for a wild-card berth under first-year coach Todd Monken, fell short on Sunday in a battle down in the bayou amid an overtime loss to the New Orleans Saints . Cleveland plans to start Watson, Houston's former franchise quarterback, but second-year passer Shedeur Sanders proved his potential by keeping the Browns alive in the Superdome. While throwing for nearly 200 yards and two touchdowns, Sanders was also sacked five times. Meanwhile, Cleveland's defense recorded five sacks, headlined by former Defensive Rookie of the Year Carson Schwesinger. "They're really good players, they're athletic and they're disruptive," Texans offensive coordinator Nick Caley said. "They've got that speed off the ball. They use their hands and they play really hard continuously. They're a handful for sure." As for Houston, quarterback C.J. Stroud threw for a season-high 384 yards and tied his career high in touchdown passes with five as Houston rolled past the Bolts in a 44-22 victory at SoFi Stadium. Despite a slow offensive start, Houston found a rhythm in the second quarter and never looked back. The Texans could be dealing with a multitude of injuries following Friday's practice. For the third straight day, rookie offensive lineman Keylan Rutledge did not practice. Running back Woody Marks and defensive ends Will Anderson Jr. and Danielle Hunter also could be in trouble after missing practice on Thursday and Friday. How do the experts feel about Sunday's showdown between a pair of AFC dark horses desperate to pick up a win for different reasons? away.headline: Texans estimate David Montgomery as a full participant, but Woody Marks doesn't practice
away.blurb: The Texans did not practice on Monday, but they were required to release an injury report ahead of Thursday night's game against the Colts. Running back David Montgomery was estimated as a full participant again, putting him on track to return this week. A groin injury has sidelined him the past four games. Linebacker Jake Hummel (groin) was listed as limited Monday. Montgomery returned to practice Thursday and was a full participant Friday, but he was inactive again Sunday. The Texans estimated linebacker Azeez Al-Shaair (groin), wide receiver Marvin Harrison Jr. (hamstring), defensive end Danielle Hunter (hamstring), tight end Brevin Jordan (foot/illness) and running back Woody Marks (concussion) as non-participants. Al-Shaair, Harrison, Hunter and Jordan did not play Sunday, and Marks was hurt in the loss to the Browns. Safety Reed Blankenship (hand), wide receiver Tank Dell (hand/shoulder), offensive tackle Blake Fisher (thumb), cornerback Kamari Lassiter (wrist), offensive guard Febechi Nwaiwu (knee), offensive lineman Keylan Rutledge (shoulder), cornerback Jaylin Smith (hamstring) and offensive guard Wyatt Teller (back) were full participants.

away.headline: Texans vs. Colts First Injury Report: Who's at Risk of Missing TNF
away.blurb: Pro Bowl linebacker Azeez Al-Shaair was also a DNP in practice with his groin injury , which is worth keeping a close eye on over the course of the week. While Monday's session was a walkthrough, his estimation marks his fourth DNP in a row. The newest name worth noting as a DNP for the Texans in practice is running back Woody Marks, who left Sunday's game in Cleveland with a concussion, and is not expected to play this coming week against the Colts. If Marks can't play as expected due to being stuck in concussion protocol, there's a good chance that Montgomery will be able to return for his first game played since he went down with his groin injury in Week 5 against the Tennessee Titans , and will have Emari Demercado backing him up as Houston's RB2. The one area of Indianapolis' roster to keep a close watch on is their secondary, as both of their starting cornerbacks, Sauce Gardner and Charvarius Ward, were estimated as DNP during their first practice of the week. We'll get a clearer picture of what to expect for the Colts and Texans' availability as the week progresses, and as both teams officially hit the field for a true practice. But based on the intel we have now, there's a good chance some big names will be forced out of the action for each side. Texans Facing RB Shortage vs. Browns With David Montgomery Out After a rough Week 10 loss to the Cleveland Browns , the Houston Texans are already beginning their preparation for their upcoming matchup against the Indianapolis Colts, which comes on a short week for Thursday Night Football. And on that short week, we already have a glimpse of the Texans and Colts' first injury report of three, which comes after both teams hosted a walkthrough on Monday with estimations of each players' practice participation. home.headline: Texans' brutal injury report just gave the Browns a golden opportunity
home.blurb: The Browns will host a banged-up Texans team that has already ruled out edge rusher Danielle Hunter, linebacker Azeez Al-Shaair, wide receiver Marvin Harrison Jr., and left guard Keylan Rutledge. Will Anderson, Houston’s superstar pass rusher, also left Thursday’s practice with an ankle injury, was a nonparticipant on Friday, and is listed as questionable along with starting right tackle Trent Brown (wrist). Cleveland, meanwhile, has no major injury concerns. Top wide receiver Denzel Boston was listed as questionable with a toe injury , but the rookie practiced on Friday and is trending toward playing. The only Browns starter ruled out for Sunday is safety Ronnie Hickman with a concussion, but the Browns are deep at that position; second-round rookie Emmanuel McNeil-Warren is slated to start Sunday’s game alongside veteran Grant Delpit. There could be openings in the middle of the field for head coach Todd Monken to exploit with tight end Harold Fannin Jr. and shifty wideout KC Concepcion. To'oTo'o is a solid linebacker for the Texans, but he’s been in and out of the lineup due to injuries himself this season and has struggled in pass coverage. Texans' brutal injury report just gave the Browns a golden opportunity Skip to main content News The Cleveland Browns are one of six NFL teams with an undefeated record in home games entering Week 10, and their chances of extending that streak just got better based on Friday’s injury report . The Browns felt like legitimate 4.5-point home underdogs for this game, especially after Houston demolished the Los Angeles Chargers in Week 9. But if Anderson joins the Texans’ inactives list on Sunday, the Browns could find themselves in prime position to pull off another upset. Texans could be missing exactly what they needed to exploit the Browns' biggest weakness The Texans were shaping up to be an extremely tough matchup for Cleveland, and they probably still are. But their defense potentially being down its top two pass rushers, along with Al-Shaair on the second level, changes everything. Anderson enters Week 10 as the NFL leader in sacks with 9.5. As a team, Houston moved into a tie for first place with the Minnesota Vikings last week. No quarterback, meanwhile, has been sacked more than Deshaun Watson, who’s been taken down 33 times in eight games. Keeping Watson upright will be one of the keys to this game regardless of who’s rushing off the edges. The Texans are one of the few teams in the NFL who have a worse rushing attack than the Browns — Houston is 29th, Cleveland is 25th — and it would behoove the Browns to play this game from ahead and force quarterback C.J. Stroud to throw from the pocket against Denzel Ward and their elite secondary. Al-Shaair’s absence is also pivotal. Without him, the Texans could have to move Henry To'oTo'o to middle linebacker or lean on a part-time player like Wade Woodaz for Sunday's game.
