home.blurb: So there's a lot to take away from the Texans' injury report. Yet, the biggest and perhaps most surprising absence that Houston will be faced with this weekend surrounds their veteran star edge rusher Danielle Hunter, who's been ruled out after logging a limited practice on Thursday and didn't participate on Friday. As to how severe Hunter's injury is long-term, we don't really know yet. All we know is that Hunter likely suffered a hamstring injury during practice on Thursday, and it's serious enough to keep him out for one week–– and possibly more, knowing that the Texans are on a short week for Week 11. Azeez Al-Shaair is out for the Texans once again, seemingly with another groin injury that's kept him limited throughout the past several weeks . Another noteworthy name from the Texans' lineup who won't be playing on Sunday: their big trade acquisition of Marvin Harrison Jr. (hamstring), who was a limited participant in Wednesday's practice, but would not suit up for Thursday or Friday. And knowing that Harrison Jr. is dealing with a hamstring issue, there's a possibility that the Texans' wideout suffered that hamstring tweak in the middle of Houston's team session on Wednesday, and will now be forced out for a period of time. Montgomery's case is simple: he's been dealing with a groin injury dating back to Week 5 against the Tennessee Titans, has been out for the past three games, but was a full practice participant on Friday, that gives him hope to finally get back on the field for Week 10. However, for Anderson Jr., he deserves a bit more attention for his situation. He was a limited participant in practice on Thursday due to an ankle issue, and would inevitably not practice on Friday as a DNP. It’s a critical game for both teams. The Packers remain in last place in the NFC North, even while winning five of their last six games. The Vikings have lost two consecutive games following a 6-0 start. Who will win the game? And, with this being the halfway point of the season, who will lead the team in rushing, receiving and sacks? And, ultimately, what will be the team’s final record and playoff fate? Here are our Packers-Vikings picks and midseason predictions. Bill Huber’s Packers-Vikings Prediction The Vikings acquired Kirk Cousins this week. It’s a huge move for the Vikings, who somehow are 6-2 despite their quarterbacks’ inability to get the ball to Justin Jefferson. Cousins has faced the Packers 10 times while with the Vikings. He topped a 110 passer rating in seven of those games. OK, but what about this season? With the Raiders, Cousins ranked fifth in passing yards, second in touchdown passes and 11th in passer rating. Plain and simple, he remains a quality starting quarterback. Initially, I had the Vikings beat the Packers 20-17. I’m perhaps guilty of overvaluing Cousins based on his stats this season and his play against Green Bay over the years, but I think he’s good enough to make the Vikings a legit contender. He’s not good enough to carry an offense, though. On Friday, the Vikings ruled out tight end T.J. Hockenson and receiver Jauan Jennings. Helped by Cousins, Hockenson caught 86 passes in 2022 and 95 passes in 2023. On Sunday, the Vikings listed receiver Jordan Addison among their inactives due to a finger injury. At full strength, few quarterbacks could match Justin Jefferson, Addison and Hockenson for a Big Three. On Sunday, Cousins will be throwing to Jefferson, receiver Tai Felton (three catches) and tight end Gavin Bartholomew (seven catches). So, let’s flip-flop the original prediction. Packers 20, Vikings 17. Bill’s Record: 7-2. Jacob Westendorf’s Packers-Vikings Prediction Yes, Kirk Cousins is back, but Green Bay's defense is for real until proven otherwise. The Packers had some answers for Brian Flores' group in Week 1 until Jordan Love was snowed under by Minnesota's pressure. This time, Lambeau Field will be the X-factor as the offensive line will be able to hear Love manipulate the line of scrimmage, which will help him make one more play than Cousins, as the Packers score a big win heading into their bye week. Score: Packers 21, Vikings 17. Jacob’s Record: 6-3. Green Bay Packers quarterback Jordan Love (10) waits for the snap against the Dallas Cowboys at Lambeau Field. | IMAGN IMAGES via Reuters Connect What Will Be Packers’ Final Record? What Will Be Packers’ Final Record? Bill: 11-6 (Losses at home to the Vikings and Bills and at the Bears). Jacob: 12-5 (Losses at home against Buffalo and at Chicago). Where Will Packers Finish in NFC North? Bill: Last (with the same record as the Vikings but by losing the tiebreaker). Jacob: Second (Chicago wins the NFC North thanks to a win on Christmas Day at Soldier Field). Who Will Lead Packers in Sacks? Bill: Lukas Van Ness. I came up with this question in light of Micah Parsons’ presumptive return for the game against the Rams. Tucker Kraft has had a quiet season following last year’s torn ACL. It’s just part of coming off a major injury. So, while I thought about going with Parsons here, Van Ness will maintain the team lead and finish with eight sacks. Jacob: Lukas Van Ness. Van Ness has 4.5 sacks, which leads the team. His job should get a little easier with Micah Parsons' return to the lineup as he'll see less double teams. Parsons is a good bet here, as well, but has noted it may take him a while to look like himself again. The goal for the Packers is going to be to have him at his best in the postseason. Who Will Lead Packers in Rushing? Green Bay Packers running back Kaleb Johnson (26) rushes the ball against the New England Patriots at Gillette Stadium. | IMAGN IMAGES via Reuters Connect Bill: Kaleb Johson leads the team with 172 rushing yards, just ahead of MarShawn Lloyd (149) and about double Josh Jacobs (80). Jacobs might only miss two games with his broken finger, meaning he’ll have five or six games to surge to the front. Bill: Kaleb Johson leads the team with 172 rushing yards, just ahead of MarShawn Lloyd (149) and about double Josh Jacobs (80). Jacobs might only miss two games with his broken finger, meaning he’ll have five or six games to surge to the front. Jacob: Kaleb Johnson leads the team in rushing, which is incredible considering how his season has gone to date. The guess here is that he's out of Matt LaFleur's doghouse and going to be a more focal point of Green Bay's offense in Josh Jacobs' absence. That will continue even when Jacobs returns to the lineup. Who Will Lead Packers in Receiving Yards? Bill: Christian Watson has 879 receiving yards, putting him on pace to blow past 1,650 yards. Matthew Golden has 783 receiving yards, putting him on pace to push for 1,500 yards. I’ll take Golden to surge to the lead, though. He has five consecutive games of six-plus catches and four consecutive games with 10-plus targets. The sheer volume of passes going to Golden will push him past the explosive play off Watson, especially if last week’s game signals that his drops are behind him. The big question: Can they set the combined yardage record? Jacob: Christian Watson. This might be one of the most intriguing storylines down the stretch. Watson and Golden are neck and neck in this category now, with Watson holding a slight advantage. Watson is used to playing this late in the season and has made some big plays in big games. Golden has, as well, so this will be really close as the season comes to a close, but give us Watson to go over 1,200 yards for the season and earn the team's receiving title. Will Jordan Love Lead NFL in Passing Yards? Bill: Entering Sunday, Cincinnati’s Joe Burrow leads the NFL with 298.3 passing yards per game. Jordan Love is hot on his heels with a 290.9-yard average. That’s less than a first down per game. Playing five consecutive cold-weather games down the stretch isn’t going to help Love in his pursuit. Jacob: Yes, the only way the Packers can move the ball is on the right arm of Jordan Love. There's little reason to believe that's going to change, even when the elements start turning colder. Add in some games that could be potential shootouts, like a home game against Buffalo or a road game against Chicago. That could cause Love to pile up some big numbers. How Will the Season End? Bill: With the entire NFC North earning their way into the playoff field, the last-place Packers will squeak into the postseason as the No. 7 seed. It’s obviously a familiar place for the Packers. And it’s a death sentence. The No. 7 seed has to play at the No. 2 seed. If the No. 7 pulls off an upset, it will have to play at the No. 1 seed. So, let’s roll with the Packers upsetting the rival Bears in the wild-card round but meeting their maker against the playoff-rival 49ers in the divisional round. Jacob: The Packers will earn the NFC's fifth seed and have a date with the NFC South-winning Tampa Bay Buccaneers in the first round of the playoffs. A big game from Jordan Love and Christian Watson, coupled with a suffocating defensive performance in which Micah Parsons will collect three sacks and a forced fumble against Baker Mayfield, will give the team its first playoff win since 2023. They will follow that by avenging last year's loss in the playoffs to the Chicago Bears by knocking them out at Soldier Field in the divisional round on a game-winning field goal from Trey Smack. Linebackers Blake Cashman (concussion) and Kyle Van Noy (calf) run the risk of missing Week 10. The Green Bay Packers are a long way removed from the team that lost to the Vikings in Week 1. Green Bay has been one of the best two-way teams since Week 6, ranking Top 10 in both EPA per play and EPA allowed in that span. This Vikings stop unit is great, but it's possibly down some key guys and playing on a short week after logging major minutes on MNF. Tucker Kraft had a nice day against the Vikings in Week 1 and has been a red zone threat in recent weeks, with two TDs in his last three games. picks.blurb: 4 Bold Predictions for Minnesota Vikings vs Green Bay Packers - Yahoo Sports Search Query for Search Search Home News Finance Sports More Mail NFL Power Rankings Fantasy Football NFL Power Rankings Week 11 Waiver Wire Chargers get first win College football Top 25 Latest NFL updates 4 Bold Predictions for Minnesota Vikings vs Green Bay Packers Minnesota Vikings NFL: Buffalo Bills at Minnesota Vikings NFL: San Francisco 49ers at Minnesota Vikings NFL: Minnesota Vikings at Tampa Bay Buccaneers NFL: Green Bay Packers at Minnesota Vikings It hasn’t always been pretty, especially offensively, but the Minnesota Vikings enter Week 10 with a 6-2 record, good for a second-place tie in the NFC North. Yet, after losing back-to-back games, the Vikings know they can reach a higher ceiling, because they were in first place for the first seven weeks of the season. The hope is that trading for Kirk Cousins can resurrect Kevin O’Connell’s previously potent scoring attacks after ranking just 27th in points this season. Yet, considering the four-time Pro Bowl QB has already operated Kevin O’Connell’s offense for two seasons, it shouldn’t take the 38-year-old long to get back in the saddle. Even though he was just acquired Tuesday, Cousins understands the importance of the Vikings’ next matchup, against the division rival Green Bay Packers, who enter the week at 6-3, in fourth place of the division. As Sunday approaches, it’s time to dive into four bold predictions for this week’s Vikings-Packers game. One person who has to be thrilled with Cousins’ return is Justin Jefferson who has seen his targets dwindle since employee No. 8 left town. Yet, Jefferson already has chemistry with Cousins, and the new Vikings QB is playing at an elite level. It may be as easy as riding a bike with Jefferson reuniting with Cousins, which could lead to the best game No. 18 has had since Week 18 of the 2024 season, when he went off for 192 yards and a touchdown. The Vikings have gotten horrid QB play all season long. While Carson Wentz and Kyler Murray had stretches where they took care of the football, they also missed several open receivers. Cousins will be much better reading the field and finding the open man. As a result, we’ll see him become the first Vikings QB to have a 300-yard game all season. He just needs to do what he's done this season for the Raiders and throughout his career, which is to distribute the football and bring a high floor to the passing game. If he can do that, the Vikings should be in every game because of their elite defense. The first test comes on Sunday afternoon at Lambeau Field, against MVP candidate Jordan Love and the Green Bay Packers. It's a massive game in the NFL's most competitive division, with the Vikings having an opportunity to complete a sweep over the Packers and secure a head-to-head tiebreaker. Here are our staff writers' score predictions. Read BMTN without the ads. BMTN Premium: The latest BMTN and BMTS stories ad-free, plus Weather+ with Sven Sundgaard. $6.99/month or $60/annual → Will Ragatz: Packers 24, Vikings 20 The Vikings absolutely can win this game, with Cousins providing a boost to the offense and Brian Flores' defense doing its thing. But it's hard to sweep a division rival, especially one as good as the Packers. Jordan Love is playing at an extremely high level right now and should have some answers to Minnesota's blitzes. I don't love that the Vikings are without Blake Cashman, who is the MVP of their defense and one of the best linebackers in football. Cousins could also have a little rust in his first week with his new/old team. For those reasons, it feels safer to pick Green Bay. Joe Nelson: Vikings 27, Packers 23 Jordan Love scares me. He's playing at an MVP level and making deep throws look as simple as a checkdown. It's truly terrifying. But Minnesota destroyed him in the second half of the season opener, and without Josh Jacobs, the Packers should be one-dimensional. That gives the NFL's best defense the edge, even if middle linebacker Blake Cashman misses the game. Meanwhile, the Vikings' offense is going to finally look functional with Kirk Cousins at quarterback. Justin Jefferson will get back to his annual routine of torching the Packers, and the Vikings will leave Lambeau Field with newfound Super Bowl hopes. Tony Liebert: Packers 31, Vikings 30 The Vikings ripped off the band-aid and made the right move to trade for Kirk Cousins, but immediately going into Lambeau Field is a tough task for any quarterback. The Packers' offense has begun to find something through the air with Matthew Golden emerging as a breakout star. I think Brian Flores will have a gameplan to get Green Bay out of its flow offensively, but the Vikings' offense also has a slow start with Cousins. The Packers will make one more play than Minnesota in a close one. Jonathan Harrison: Vikings 21, Packers 15 Jordan Love is playing at an unreal level lately. So has the Vikings' defense this season. Which wins out? That will come down to how well the Vikings' offense operates. With Kirk back, the offense is expected to just be fixed. However, he's practiced twice this week. That's not a lot of time to get settled back in. If he's able to just keep the offense on the field and sustain drives, then the Vikings' defense will be able to stay healthy and make Love's day miserable. I think that is the likeliest scenario. It won't be pretty, but it will be encouraging going forward as Kirk gets reacquainted with KOC's offense. The Vikings may have taken steps to fix their abysmal offense, but Rome wasn't rebuilt in a day, or something. I have an inkling that, under the hood, the dysfunction runs deeper than just the signal caller, so I expect the defense will once again be on the field long enough for them to tire, and for Jordan Love to find Christian Watson and Matthew Golden in space one too many times. away.headline: LaFleur provides injury updates on Micah Parsons, Kevin Zeitler and others after loss to Vikings
away.blurb: During his day after press conference on Monday, Green Bay Packers coach Matt LaFleur provided several injury updates coming out of Sunday's loss to the Minnesota Vikings . Among the players mentioned: Micah Parsons, who could return next week against Los Angeles Rams ; Kevin Zeitler, who was the planned starter at right guard against the Vikings; and Brandon Cisse, who exited the loss with a ribs injury. On CB Brandon Cisse: LaFleur was confident Cisse, who went out of Sunday's game with a ribs injury, will NOT miss significant time. He was injured after colliding with Myles Price on the Vikings' shocking 38-yard touchdown pass on 3rd-and-23 in the first half. Cisse did not return to the game, and Carrington Valentine played the rest of the way. On EDGE Micah Parsons : LaFleur said his plan is for Parsons to make his long-awaited return to the field against the Rams next Wednesday, but he still has a "couple more hurdles" to clear before LaFleur can definitively say Parsons will play in Week 12. The 21-day practice window for the All-Pro edge rusher is open until Nov. 25. Last week, Parsons got in his first 11-on-11 reps. The updates from LaFleur on Monday: On G Kevin Zeitler: LaFleur said the plan was for Zeitler to start at right guard, but he suffered a "freak" triceps injury at practice late in the week and wasn't healthy enough to play against the Vikings, although he was "fighting" the coaches to play. Zeitler didn't practice on Friday and was inactive on Sunday. Travis Glover started at right guard for an offensive line that imploded against Brian Flores and the Vikings. On WRs Bo Melton and Skyy Moore: LaFleur said he believes Melton is fine after injuring his thigh against the Vikings, while he's waiting until the end of the week to see how Moore's ankle responds to another injury. Moore previously missed four games while on injured reserve after hurting his ankle in Week 5. away.headline: Chris Long says he’s ‘never’ seen another NFL team do what the Vikings are doing right now
away.blurb: The Minnesota Vikings had a dream return for Kirk Cousins, as they dominated the Green Bay Packers, but how they are doing it is surprising. Cousins might have stood out, but the way the Vikings performed overall had more to do with more than just Cousins' contribution. Chris Long says he’s ‘never’ seen another NFL team do what the Vikings are doing right now - Yahoo Sports Search Query for Search Search Home News Finance Sports More Mail NFL Photo by Jerry Holt/The Minnesota Star Tribune via Getty Images Vatsal Gupta · HITC Tue, November 17, 2026 at 1:27 PM UTC · 2 min read Advertisement Advertisement About Our Ads The 30-10 win for the Minnesota Vikings was powered by Kirk Cousins returning in style, completing 21/31 passes, gaining 207 yards, and throwing two touchdowns. In fact, Chris Long says that what the Vikings did against the Packers is something he has never seen before. Chris Long on Minnesota Vikings surprising him The Vikings were shredded by the Buffalo Bills before this game against the Packers, and an away game just after was not going to be easy. However, the way the Vikings took control of the defence, more than the offence, was startling to see, with the pace of their game off the charts. Cousins dictated the proceedings, but for a team that played 80 snaps against the Bills in a tough loss less than a week ago, the intensity was surprising against the Packers. Long said [via Green Light with Chris Long ]: "So, I think Kirk Cousins is the big story in this game for everybody, right? It's like, what a difference a quarterback can make. But, to me, y'all, I think the story is how lightning-fast the Minnesota Vikings look defensively. They're coming off six days' rest. They played 80 plays on Monday night against the Buffalo Bills. "I've never seen a team where you look at the numbers and say, "Hey, man, maybe it's not their week." They played 80 snaps against a physical Buffalo team, and it's been an emotional whirlwind for them. I know Kirk put some wind in their sails, but they're going to Green Bay, and they're playing a very good defence and an offence that shredded them for eight explosive plays. Jordan Love has been one of the best quarterbacks in the NFL against the blitz. "Dude, they look like they were playing that game at home." The Vikings look energised, with the Cousins trade sending a surge of electricity through the team, translating to an intense performance. It will be interesting to see how they fare once the initial euphoria of this move fades away, but seeing how well they are executing on the thankless side of the game, it would be hard to bet against them.

home.headline: Micah Parsons Injury, Timeline Updated by Packers' HC as Star Still Has 'Hurdles to Clear'
home.blurb: Micah Parsons is on track to return to the field for the Green Bay Packers before Thanksgiving. Packers head coach Matt LaFleur said the team plans on having the star pass-rusher available for its Week 12 game against the Los Angeles Rams on Wednesday, Nov. 25, even though he still has a "couple more hurdles to clear," per ESPN's Adam Schefter . Parsons' return will give the Packers a much-needed boost, as he is one of the best defensive players in the league with a resume that includes three First-Team All-Pro selections, five Pro Bowl nods and five seasons with double-digit sacks. It seems like that return is on track for the next time the team takes the field. LaFleur also said Green Bay will "see where he is by the end of the week." Parsons hasn't played this season as he recovers from a torn ACL he suffered in December. He missed the rest of the 2025 campaign for Green Bay, including its postseason loss to the rival Chicago Bears. However, he might finally be on the field again for the NFC North club, which opened his practice window earlier this month. Green Bay is on a bye for Week 11, so he has a bit more time to get ready for a Wednesday game. This is also a critical time for the Packers in the postseason chase, as Sunday's loss to the Minnesota Vikings dropped them to 6-4 and in last place in the competitive NFC North. Every other team in the division has just two losses, so the focus may eventually have to shift to the wild-card race. And that game against the Rams is a critical one. Green Bay, Los Angeles and the Seattle Seahawks are all 6-4 and tied in the race for the seventh and final seed in the NFC playoff picture. The Packers have the spot as of Monday because of conference record, but a head-to-head result against the Rams will go a long way toward determining wild-card positioning.

home.blurb: LP = Limited participant in practice. DNP = Did not participate in practice. Probable = the league defines a Probable injury designation as a 75% or greater chance of playing. Historically, 95% of players designated probable are active and played on game day. Questionable = the league defines a Questionable injury designation as being ‘uncertain’ of whether the player will play or not. This replaces the former definition of having a 50% chance of playing. Historically, 70-75% of players with a Questionable injury designation were active and played on game day. Doubtful = The league defines a Doubtful injury designation to mean the player is unlikely to participate in the game. In practical terms, teams use the designation when a player has less than a 50% chance to suit up, and active game appearances from this designation remain rare. Historically only around 6% of players with a Doubtful designation are active and played on game day. Out = will not play. Players with this designation are not active on game day and league rules prohibit them from playing. For the Vikings, no change in injury status for anybody compared to Wednesday’s estimates. That doesn’t bode well for any of the players that have yet to practice this week being available on Sunday. We’ll see if there are any upgrades tomorrow, but otherwise it looks like in addition to Blake Cashman, Hockenson, Ingram-Dawkins, Jennings, and Van Noy may not be available on Sunday. But the Jaguars can't afford to focus on anything about seeding, the AFC, or their new pieces when 1 p.m. comes along. The Jaguars are set to battle a Tennessee Titans team that has played its best football of the season over the last three weeks, losing two one-score games against teams with winning records and earning their first win of the season in Week 6 on the road against the Indianapolis Colts. The Jaguars, sitting at 6-2 after back-to-back post-bye week wins, will need a road win in Nashville to keep their own momentum. That momentum got a jolt over the week with trade deadline additions of Jordan Davis, Jessie Bates III, and Davon Godchaux, but the Jaguars believe they have kept their eyes on the ball during their preparation for the week. “I think sometimes when you maybe make a player acquisition like this, and you get some star power, you get some big names and things like that, I think maybe there's a – I've seen in the past some teams that, like almost kind of, ‘Oh, okay, we're good now. And those guys will make the play.’ And I don't think that's how our building operated at all when that news broke," Jaguars head coach Liam Coen said this week. "It was almost just like, ‘Alright, we know we're a good team. We know we're a good team and these players are only here to help us take it to the next level.’ But we're not going to sit back and say, ‘Okay, well, Jessie Bates will make the play or Jordan Davis and Davon, they'll make the play. We don't have to go and do it.’ I think our guys have a lot of pride in the way that they prepare, the way that they practice." How do the national predictions see this one playing out, however? We take a look below. Sports Illustrated Albert Breer: Jaguars Eva Geitheim: Jaguars Mitch Goldich: Jaguars Mike Kadlick: Jaguars Gilbert Manzano: Jaguars Conor Orr: Jaguars John Pluym: Jauars Matt Verderame: Jaguars Matt Bowen: Jaguars Mike Clay: Jaguars Jeremy Fowler: Jaguars Dan Graziano: Jaguars Kalyn Kahler: Jaguars Pamela Maldonado: Jaguars Eric Moody: Jaguars Jason Reid: Jaguars Ben Solak: Jaguars Lindsey Thiry: Jaguars Seth Wickersham: Titans Jeremy Bergman: Jaguars Brooke Cersosimo: Jaguars Gennaro Filice: Jaguars Bobby Kownack: Jaguars Dan Parr: Jaguars Joe Buscaglia: Jaguars Jon Greenberg: Jaguars Larry Holder: Jaguars Nick Kosmider: Jaguars Josh Kendal: Jaguars Austin Mock: Jaguars Jacksonville Jaguars On SI Analysis The Jaguars do not get the sweep here, earning 29 of 30 votes. Still, that is quite an easy summary of what people expect to happen in this one. The Jaguars are one of the AFC's best teams and have been the most-talked-about team of the trade deadline week after their all-in moves, though two of the three defenders they traded for will not appear against the Titans. Even without Jordan Davis and Jessie Bates III on hand , the Jaguars will have a high standard on defense. The Jaguars do not like how many rushing yards they allowed to the Baltimore Ravens last week, just like they didn't like the fact that they didn't complete the shutout against the Indianapolis Colts in Week 8. With that in mind, they are facing a Titans team that has played much better offensively as of late. The Titans offense has flirted with being ranked in the top-half of teams in terms of both offensive EPA/Play and Success Rate after their big scoring outputs against the Cleveland Browns and Cincinnati Bengals. Cam Ward is playing better after early-season struggles, and Tony Pollard has been amongst the NFL's most productive runners over the last few weeks. This isn't the hapless Titans offense from the start of the year, even without Carnell Tate. But the Jaguars' defense simply feels like it has been hitting on all cylinders. The only quarterbacks to really have success against them this season in terms of moving the ball have been CJ Stroud and Joe Burrow, and Ward is not that. The Jaguars can't afford to treat the Titans like the Ravens a week ago, but this should still be a game that they control. On the other side of the ball, the Titans have lost their two best defenders in Jeffery Simmons and Amani Hooker due to trades, and the numbers have reflected it. It does not feel like their secondary should be able to keep up with the Jaguars, and I am going Jacksonville 34, Titans 12 in this one. picks.headline: 5 Bold Predictions for Jaguars vs. Titans: Which New Addition Makes the First Big Play
picks.blurb: 5 Bold Predictions for Jaguars vs. Titans: Which New Addition Makes the First Big Play Skip to main content SI.COM Betting Sites Sportsbook Promos BetMGM Bonus Code Fanatics Sportsbook Promo Canada Sportsbook Promos bet365 CA Bonus Code Rainbet Promo Code Stake Promo Code PREDICTION MARKETS College Market Prediction Market Apps Prediction Market Promos Kalshi Promo Code Kalshi Referral Code Apps like Kalshi Polymarket Promo Code Polymarket Referral Code Novig Promo Code Underdog Promo Code Stadium Wonders Digital Covers Push Notifications Digital Subscription Customer Service Prospects by SI JACKSONVILLE, Fla. -- After a frantic start to the week that saw the Jacksonville Jaguars make the biggest moves of this year's NFL Trade Deadline, it is worth remember that the Jaguars do, in fact, have an opponent on Sunday. The 6-2 Jaguars are set to travel to Nissan Stadium to face the Tennessee Titans in Week 10, their first game since making blockbuster trades for Jessie Bates and Jordan Davis, along with adding Davon Godchaux for a sixth-round pick. For a Jaguars team that has their eyes set on an AFC South title and a top seed in the playoffs, they are treating the Titans with the same seriousness that they treated the Indianapolis Colts and Baltimore Ravens over the last two weeks. So, how do we see the Jaguars' Week 10 battle with the Titans playing out? We break it down below. Jessie Bates Records An Interception While it certainly remains to be seen if the Jaguars will actually play any of their new defensive pieces against the Titans, I believe they will. Jakobi Meyers and Greg Newsome each played in their first games with the franchise last season after joining the team during that same week, and I think that means we see the trio make their Jaguars debuts. In the process, I think we see Bates create his first Jaguars takeaway right off the bat. Cam Ward is far from the most turnover-prone quarterback the Jaguars have played this season; that distinction goes to Daniel Jones. But he is right near the league average in interception rate, and he has made some egregious decisions with the ball over his last two seasons as a starter. This feels like the perfect week for Anthony Campanile to cook some pressure looks up to confuse Ward, and Bates is a natural playmaker. I think we see his impact right away. Parker Washington Catches 2 TDs The Titans' defense has been ... not very good against slot receivers this season. The Titans rank in the bottom-5 in the NFL against slot targets in each of the following categories: yards per play allowed, yards after the catch allowed, yards after the catch over expectation, and average seperation. The Titans have simply been a mess in the slot, even moving long-time outside cornerback Alontae Taylor to the slot despite signing him in March to play on the outside. As a result, I think this is a Parker Washington week. He is the clear No. 1 receiver in the offense, and I think he shakes off some inconsistent moments we have seen as of late and has a huge game against the Titans. Washington is due for a big performance, and I think we see it this Sunday against the Titans. Cam Ward Throws For Fewer Than 150 Yards There have been 275 quarterback performances this season. In just 39 of those performances, we have seen quarterbacks throw for fewer than 150 yards. Cam Ward makes up two of those games, a number that is trumped only by Bo Nix and Malis Willis which is, well, not great company to be in as far as productive gunslingers go. Ward has been more productive and explosive as of late and is coming off one of the best games of his career, but I predict the Jaguars limit Ward to under 150. Ward threw for just 141 yards against the Jaguars in Week 13 a year ago, and the Jaguars limited Daniel Jones and Joe Fagnano to a combined 189 yards over the last eight quarters. The Jaguars' pass defense is clicking, largely due to the work of defensive coordinator Anthony Campanile, and I believe we see it continue this week. Jaguars Limit Tony Pollard to Under 4.0 YPC Titans running back Tony Pollard has been on a tear over the last few weeks. Pollard, who has rushed for 246 yards and five touchdowns over the last two games, broke out of a mid-season skid and has been able to average over 4.0 yards per carry in every single game but two this season. While Pollard has been one of the NFL's more impressive runners over the last few weeks, I expect the Jaguars to be ready to bottle him up on Sunday. Again, I think the Jaguars will play Davis and Godchaux on Sunday. But even if they don't, I do not think the Titans have the offense to keep the Jaguars off-balance enough to run the ball on them. Teams can only run the ball on the Jaguars when the Jaguars are threatened by the early-down pass, and I do not see the Titans having much success there. Walker Little Pitches Another Shutout The Jaguars have seen Walker Little play really, really well over the last few weeks since stepping into the lineup for an injured Anton Harrison. According to NextGenStats, Little has allowed pressure on just 6.4% of his pass blocks, the fifth lowest rate in the league among left tackles (minimum 100 pass blocks). On his 109 pass blocks, his 87.2% 1-on-1 matchup rate is the highest in the league among left tackles; his 6.3% 1-on-1 pressure rate allowed is the third lowest pressure rate allowed in the league. “The experience always helps. Confidence is a heck of a thing, and I think he's the one that said it in an interview that humility helped. Where obviously he became our swing tackle, and all that guy has done is just stay the course," Jaguars head coach Liam Coen said on Wednesday. "Like, never got up, too down. He's just very steady. I really like Walker's play demeanor, the look in his eye recently and not taking everything so seriously. He's able to have fun with it. He's out there playing a game that he loves and competes with, but he's playing at a high level right now. He's got confidence, and you can tell.” Little will mostly draw Titans pass-rusher Jacob Martin, who has had a good year. But after strong showings against the Houston Texans' pass-rush duo in London a month ago and then a dominant outing against Trey Hendrickson last week , I think Little has the edge entering Week 10. He is playing some of the best football of his career right now, and I predict it leads to another shutout. The Jacksonville Jaguars, one of the most active buyers at the trade deadline, are coming to Nashville to boast their new pickups. The last time Tennessee faced Jacksonville, the Titans lost 41-7 at the very end of the 2025 season. Cam Ward missed the majority of that game after exiting early with a shoulder injury, and his healthy showing tomorrow is the key to a potential Titans upset. Will: Cam Ward stays hot in Carnell Tate's return Ward nearly led Tennessee to a victory over the (now) 6-2 Cincinnati Bengals in Week 8. The Titans falling short 36-43 in overtime was partly due to Ward taking a costly sack late in regulation, but the QB can't at all be blamed for losing a game he kept Tennessee in. With WR1 Carnell Tate trending toward a return, Ward should have all of his weapons in place to put up another promising game. The Titans even kept RB Tony Pollard at the deadline for Ward's own sake. Again, Jacksonville bulked up at the deadline - their defense specifically - but Tennessee leaving the offense untouched said loud and clear that this franchise believes in Ward. With a newly-gutted defense, the Titans will be relying on Ward to try and secure the win. Won't: Jaguars' overhauled defense clicks immediately Directly opposing Ward is that new-look Jags defense. In addition to adding All-Pro S Jessie Bates III, Jacksonville also acquired defensive tackles Jordan Davis and Davon Godchaux. Two out of the next three weeks, the Titans stand in the way. The south-most AFC South team sold off a ton of draft potential to make this happen, but the 6-2 team got a whole lot better as they sprint toward a hopeful Super Bowl appearance. Two out of the next three weeks, the Titans stand in the way. FOX Sports already had Jacksonville listed as a top 10 defensive team in the NFL prior to these trades. If Tennessee falls short (as is likely expected), it will be because the Jaguars' defense put a stopper in Ward and the offense's growth. That could be one reason among many, but it seems to be the most relevant by far regarding this specific matchup. Prediction: Titans lose, 34-23 At the end of the day on Sunday, I expect Jacksonville will overwhelm Tennessee. I don't believe it will be in blowout fashion, and this is primarily because of the stable flashes of progress Ward showed in Week 8. But between their overhauled defense and Trevor Lawrence manning things under center on offense, the Titans are truly facing a championship contender this week. Perhaps the home field will help blunt the blow, as well as the team debuting their Music City jerseys. I love the jerseys. I like what we saw from Cam Ward in his most recent game. But this Jaguars team has the AFC South in a headlock, and the 1-7 Titans simply don't have enough on paper to climb out of a double-digit projected loss in this one. home.headline: Titans announce unfortunate injury news for rookie WR Carnell Tate
home.blurb: Tennessee Titans rookie wide receiver Carnell Tate missed the first game of his NFL career in Week 8, ruled out with a shoulder injury. The Titans officially ruled Tate out for Sunday’s Week 10 matchup against the Jacksonville Jaguars. With Tate out again this weekend, Cam Ward and the Tennessee offense will continue to lean on Wan’Dale Robinson, Chimere Dike, Elic Ayomanor and Calvin Ridley as their WR options. Tate, the No. 4 overall pick in the 2026 NFL Draft, had an extra week to recover over the Titans’ bye. However, he was unable to take the practice field for any action this week as he continues to deal with the lingering issue. “I was really optimistic going through the bye week. It’s just, the shoulder’s stuck on him a little bit,” head coach Robert Saleh said when speaking to reporters on Friday. “We’re hopeful for next week, but I’ll have a better answer for you guys come Wednesday.” After a relatively slow start to his NFL career, Tate exploded for 145 yards on nine catches in a Week 4 matchup against the Baltimore Ravens. The former Ohio State standout logged his first professional touchdown in a win over the Indianapolis Colts in Week 6. Through seven games in his first season with the Titans, Tate has 34 catches for 413 yards and one score. Sunday’s game against the Jaguars will kick off at 1 p.m. ET. The Dolphins will go into the game with a 1-7 record but after giving playoff contenders New England and Detroit a battle before losing at Hard Rock Stadium the past two weeks. That, of course, with quarterback Malik Willis and standout defensive lineman Zach Sieler in the lineup, with both now on injured reserve. The Colts also have their issues, having traded four veterans — Quenton Nelson, DeForrest Buckner, Keenan Allen and Josh Downs — in the midst of a wildly disappointing season that's already seen GM Chris Ballard lose his job. The Colts did retain star running back Jonathan Taylor and veteran defensive tackle Grove Stewart, who had been rumored to be on the move, and it's not like they're playing for draft position since their 2027 first-round pick belongs to the New York Jets as the result of the Sauce Gardner trade that keeps looking worse every day. Indianapolis is favored by 3.5 points, according to the Fan Duel Sportsbook . This is the second consecutive year the teams will face each other, the 2025 meeting coming in the season opener when the Colts humbled the Dolphins, 33-8, in a game that set the stage for Miami's disappointing 7-10 season that produced the regime change and rebuilding project that's going on right now. That season-opening win was part of a fantastic start for the Colts, who once were 8-2 and very much looking like legit AFC contenders. The bottom then fell out and it hasn't stopped falling out, Indianapolis losing 14 of its past 16 games going back to last November 23. This is why the Dolphins are being given a chance — even predicted by some — to win the game Sunday despite having a quarterback on his third team in two years ready to play his first real NFL snaps. The Colts gave Dallas all it could handle last week before losing in overtime, and they may benefit from the uncertainty of their roster being done now that the NFL trade deadline has passed. From this end, it's just difficult to give the Dolphins the nod here with an unproven quarterback who will have to work with the same subpar supporting cast that's hampered Willis so far this season, and without Aaron Brewer out on top of everyhing. The Dolphins defense probably will be able to keep the score close, but we'd still call it something like 20-10 for the Colts. The Colts made a few trades this week, but elected to keep Jonathan Taylor. Perhaps he can help them end a five-game losing streak. Miami picked up its first win of the season a few weeks ago at MetLife Stadium over the Jets, but has since lost to the Patriots and Lions. The Colts beat the Dolphins 33-8 early last season. Using the latest odds and analysis, here’s where I’m leaning for this Week 10 matchup with a final score prediction. Dolphins vs. Colts Odds, Spread and Total Odds via DraftKings Sportsbook Dolphins +3.5 (-105) Colts -3.5 (-115) Dolphins: +160 38.5 (Over -108/Under -112) Line Movement: The line has moved an important point from -2.5 to -3.5 since the odds opened for this game, with the total dropping a bit from 42.5 to 38.5 after the deadline. Dolphins vs. Colts Final Score Prediction SI Betting’s Iain MacMillan broke down this game in his Road to 272 Bets column, in which he picks each game every week: The Colts are bad and are certainly worth fading most weeks this season, but being only 2.5-point home favorites against the worst team in the NFL is a bit insulting. The Colts at least have some talent, especially on offense, while the Dolphins seem to be mailing it in this season. The Dolphins scored a measly nine points while gaining only 4.6 yards per play against the Lions' abysmal defense last week, which is a bad sign for them moving forward. The Colts can at least still run the football, and now they'll be able to really ride Jonathan Taylor as the Dolphins rank 29th in both opponent rush EPA and opponent rush success rate. That's enough for me to take the Colts with the spread set at less than a field goal. Pick: Colts -2.5 (-105) via DraftKings I weirdly have quite a bit of confidence in the Colts this week after keeping Jonathan Taylor at the deadline. He alone gives them the upper hand against Miami, and I think this could be a feel-good win for the Colts this week. (Photo by Carmen Mandato/Getty Images) | Getty Images David Fucillo · SB Nation Sun, November 15, 2026 at 1:50 PM UTC · 5 min read Advertisement Advertisement About Our Ads College Sports Sports Business Women's Sports College & High School Adventure Sports What & How To Watch Responsible Gaming Share Your Feedback About Our Ads The Miami Dolphins are back on the field today, heading north to Indiana to face the Indianapolis Colts. Both teams are in contention for the first-overall pick in the 2027 NFL Draft, and both have made major roster changes over the past week. The Colts made several trades ahead of the deadline this past Tuesday, sending veteran players around the league and receiving draft picks in exchange. The Dolphins stood pat at the deadline, but saw quarterback Malik Willis and defensive tackle Zach Sieler, both starters and captains, land on injured reserve. Willis has a groin injury that is expected to keep him out for a few weeks, though season-ending surgery has not been completely ruled out. Sieler ruptured his biceps muscle during the team's Week 9 game against the Detroit Lions, played through the injury for the rest of the contest, but will now require several months of rehab following surgery. Miami enters today with a 1-7 record and is in position to claim the third-overall spot in the 2027 Draft. The Colts are2-7 and in the fourth position, though they do not hold their pick after trading it to the New York Jets for cornerback Sauce Gardner last year. The Los Angeles Chargers are 0-8 and in the top spot for the spring's college prospect selection process while the 1-7 Tennessee Titans are in the second spot. How will Sunday's game play out? Both teams have to adjust to the recent roster changes. The oddsmakers at FanDuel Sportsbook seem to think the Colts are in a better position to pull off those adjustments and come away with the victory this afternoon. Phins up! Dive into game day on the SB Nation app! Celebrate every score and talk through every twist and turn with fellow Dolphins fans in real time. Join the live game chat Browse with fewer ads Seamlessly explore communities Enjoy faster commenting and posting Download the SB Nation app on iOS or Android . Dolphins at Colts (-3.5) This game feels like a matchup between a team that embraced a complete roster rebuild heading into 2026 and a team surprised to have been forced into a rebuild during 2026. Miami knew who they were entering the season as: stripping their roster down, filling it with younger players, and accepting that this season might be tough, but positioning themselves for future success. The Colts came into 2026 looking to compete in the AFC South; after back-to-back 8-9 seasons, Indianapolis was expecting to take a step forward. Instead, everything seems to have gone wrong for the Colts. That all said, Indianapolis now welcomes a Dolphins team with a first-year quarterback making his NFL debut after being a sixth-round pick in 2025 by the Philadelphia Eagles but spending the entire season on the practice squad. There are a lot of obstacles for the Dolphins in this game, and it feels like the Colts will be able to cover the 3.5 points – though it may end up closer than people think if Miami can get their running game established early. Ollie Gordon II rushing yards: 72.5 Over: -113 Under: -113 Miami's offensive system this year was built around the run – first with De'Von Achane and now with Ollie Gordon II serving as the feature back. Gordon is only averaging 57.9 yards per game, but that includes Week 1 with no carries and Week 2 with three attempts for seven yards. Since becoming the starter in Week 4, Gordon is averaging 83 yards per game, which would be seventh in the league. Miami, with a first-time starting quarterback under center today, will rely on Gordon and the running game. The Colts will throw everything they can to stop the rushing attack, but Miami will have to commit to it and find ways to create space for Gordon. He should be able to top 72.5 yards. Kyle McCord passing touchdowns: 0.5 Over : -188 Under: +142 I like the +142 you could get with the under, but one passing touchdown seems plausible, especially if the Colts stack the box to try to stop Gordon. Then again, the Dolphins didn't score a single touchdown last week against the Lions, so Miami could be held without a passing touchdown this week. I still lean toward the Dolphins finding a way to get McCord his first touchdown pass and build his confidence as the starter. Caleb Douglas receiving yards: 42.5 Douglas is averaging 15.6 yards per reception in his rookie season. If he sticks to that average, the question is whether he will get three receptions. If the Colts are stacking the box to stop Gordon and the running game, McCord should be able to find some space to get the ball to Douglas. I will take the over here, thinking it is a solid but not spectacular day for Douglas. Chop Robinson to record a sack Daniel Jones is tied for the fifth-most sacks taken this year (we will ignore that he is tied with Malik Willis). He has been pulled down 24 times. The Dolphins defense seemed to break out last week against Detroit, and they know they will have to carry the game again this week, with a backup quarterback making not just his first NFL start, but his first regular-season appearance. Robinson should set the tone and get after Jones early and often. He cannot sell out and give up on trying to contain the Colts rushing attack, but he has to make an impression and there is no better way than getting an early sack. I will take the Yes here. away.headline: Dolphins Hit With Unfortunate Aaron Brewer News in Latest Injury Report
away.blurb: The only other player who has now been hit with a DNP (did not participate) is rookie wide receiver Chris Bell. Bell is still dealing with a knee injury, which is connected to his torn ACL that he suffered at the end of his collegiate career in 2025. Bell has appeared on the injury report off and on since returning in Week 1 to play, and now he was downgraded from a limited participant on Wednesday to DNP on Thursday. Long snapper Tucker Addington (shoulder), cornerback Darrell Baker Jr. (knee ), edge Malik Herring (neck), tight end Will Kacmarek (quad/knee), and wide receiver Jared Wayne (quad) were all limited. Some good news in these listed players is that Kacmarek was upgraded to limited after missing Thursday's practice. Baker also remains limited, which could mean that he is not yet ready to play. The cornerback has made his return to practice after not playing in 2026 due to suffering a knee injury in training camp. There is still a chance that Baker could play, but the usual case is that players who remain limited likely need a week or so more to fully get back to being able to take the field. Wright has been dealing with a quad injury that led to him being ruled out in Week 9. Now, he is set to return against the Colts. Dolphins Hit With Unfortunate Aaron Brewer News in Latest Injury Report - Yahoo Sports Search Query for Search Search Home News Finance Sports More Mail NFL Dolphins Hit With Unfortunate Aaron Brewer News in Latest Injury Report (David Brytus-Imagn Images) James Brizuela · Roundtable Sports Thu, November 12, 2026 at 10:22 PM UTC · 3 min read Advertisement Advertisement About Our Ads The Miami Dolphins have released their second injury report of Week 10, and things are not looking good for center Aaron Brewer. Brewer has now missed his second straight practice, as he is currently in concussion protoco l. It is not unlikely that he will suit up against the Indianapolis Colts. The full injury report is as follows: Running back Kaytron Allen (quad), safety Michael Taaffe (wrist), safety Dante Trader Jr. (shoulder/groin), and running back Jaylen Wright (quad) were all full participants yet again. Despite the semblance of a laundry list of injured players, the Dolphins look to be in decent shape. Losing Brewer will be a huge hit to the offense, but Andrew Meyer will be there to step in. Meyer spoke on Thursday about not only learning from "the best center in the league" but also stating that he has the confidence to step in for the Miami offensive line if that is what happens. The Dolphins are looking for their second win of the season, as they will face the struggling Colts. Indianapolis may not be a pushover opponent, but they also got rid of many players at the trade deadline, leaving this to be a potential "easier" matchup for Miami.

Coach Jeff Hafley said Andrew Meyer will start in Brewer's place. Meyer, who started a game last season, has worked closely with Kyle McCord since the quarterback's arrival from Green Bay. McCord will be making his first NFL start in place of Malik Willis, who is on injured reserve. "He's done a nice job. Have a lot of confidence in Meyer," Hafley said. away.headline: Miami Dolphins’ Most Valuable Player | Week Ten | Youth
away.blurb: The Miami Dolphins have been going through a bit of a youth-movement this season, in case you haven’t heard. They’re the youngest team in the National Football League by a wide margin — with an average age of just over 25 years at the start of the season. They’ve also had the most snaps taken by rookie players out of any NFL team this season — leading the Cleveland Browns by a comfortable amount. “Definitely felt good. Really just reading my keys. Once the quarterback scrambles, he’s looking to get the ball out of his hands. That’s kind of something we talked about throughout the week. When we get him off-schedule, it’s an opportunity. Really just making the most of my opportunity in that situation.” That emphasis on developing young players is paying off for the Dolphins in a major way. While the team is currently struggling in the standings — winning just one game on the year so far — their rookies are taking their lumps and learning the ropes at an expedited pace. That should help the team progress much quicker than most anticipate, while keeping their future cap situation in the good (and cheap) place. Miami Dolphins Week Nine MVP – Cornerback Chris Johnson One young player who has been excelling in Jeff Halfey’s defensive scheme is rookie first-rounder Chris Johnson. Miami’s young cornerback has two interceptions on the season after nabbing one against Daniel Jones of the Colts on Sunday. He returned that interception 59-yards for a touchdown — Miami’s first pick-6 on the year. In addition to his two interceptions, Johnson also has a forced fumble during his rookie campaign. Following the game, Johnson spoke about how coaching helped him make his stellar play on Sunday. Week Eight – EDGE Chop Robinson

away.blurb: Miami has worked out several kickers over the past few weeks, giving them an idea of who is available to replace Gonzalez. Tuesday is typically tryout day in the NFL, and Miami will likely bring in a few kickers to audition before signing someone later in the day. The Splash Zone returns this morning to collect all the latest news, updates, and rumors in one place for you. Check out the collection below: More bad news hits Miami’s trenches as another defensive lineman is ruled out for the remainder of the year. You’ve played it on SB Nation’s website. Now check it out on the SB Nation app! Want to join in the conversation and share your thoughts or point of view on the Dolphins? Check out The Feed , our community-driven discussion about the Dolphins, football, or just about anything on your mind. You can find the feed on the front page of The Phinsider. Jump in now to advance the Dolphins discussion. The Miami Dolphins lost to the Indianapolis Colts in Week 10, with much of the postgame focus on the two missed field goals and a missed extra point by kicker Zane Gonzalez. Special teams have been inconsistent for much of the 2026 season in Miami, but missing seven points’ worth of kicks in a two-point loss was beyond even the normal inconsistency. On Monday, Miami moved on from Gonzalez, the second kicker they have cut this year. Gonzalez signed with the Dolphins as a free agent during the offseason, with the coaches looking to bring competition to incumbent kicker Riley Patterson. Gonzalez landed on injured reserve at the start of August, however, and was later released in exchange for an injury settlement. Miami began the season with Patterson, but released him in late October, re-signing Gonzalez to the practice squad. After three games as an elevated practice squad member, Gonzalez was added to the Dolphins’ 53-man roster for the Colts game – and now Miami will be looking for their third kicker this year. The waiving of Gonzalez was one part of a busy day for the Dolphins. The news around the team continued to review the Colts game, update injuries, including a season-ending injury to defensive tackle Zeek Biggers, and look at the rookies after 10 weeks. home.blurb: Edwards, 6-1, 201 pounds, has spent time on the team's active roster and practice squad this season. He was elevated in Week 8 at Jacksonville and Week 9 vs. Dallas and registered one special teams tackle. As a rookie in 2025, Edwards played in 14 games (five starts) and registered 24 tackles (18 solo), three passes defensed and two special teams stops. He was originally signed by the Colts as an undrafted free agent on May 9, 2025, out of Tulane. Toure, 6-1, 196 pounds, has played in 23 career games (two starts) in his time with the Philadelphia Eagles (2026), New Orleans Saints (2025), Denver Broncos (2025), Chicago Bears (2024-25) and Green Bay Packers (2022-24). He has compiled 14 receptions for 163 yards (11.6 avg.) and one touchdown. Toure was originally selected by the Packers in the seventh round (258th overall) of the 2022 NFL Draft out of Nebraska. His name is pronounced suh-MORE-ee TOO-ray. The Panthers have been on a downturn, as a rash of injuries has crippled them on both sides of the ball. However, just as everyone seemed to go down at once, they're now returning as a group. Here are our staff picks and predictions for Week 10's grudge match between the New Orleans Saints and Carolina Panthers . An early lead on the NFC South title is on the line between two teams that just might be the best squads in the NFL's worst division. Getting a win is always important, but it could be crucial as the Saints look to keep their season alive and attack the back half of their schedule. Saints 25, Panthers 24 This should be a close one; we've got an overachieving Panthers team running up against a Saints team that can't figure out how to play with a lead. New Orleans has gotten the better of Bryce Young over the years and they did sweep Carolina last season but we'll have to see if that translates. If the Panthers can take advantage of a beaten-up Saints offensive line (they'll be without Pro Bowl center Erik McCoy and first-round right tackle Taliese Fuaga, with rookie fourth-round pick Jeremiah Wright starting at right guard), it'll be a long afternoon for Tyler Shough. We'll guess the return of Travis Etienne Jr. at running back and Jordyn Tyson's emergence at wide receiver makes enough of a difference to win the day. Bold prediction: This game goes to overtime, too, but Tyson comes down with the game-winning score. -- John Sigler Saints 31, Panthers 17 Despite Carolina's lofty ranking against the pass, I love the matchup in favor of the Saints. The right side of the New Orleans line is a huge concern, but I think the Saints can run the ball with some success to their left and set up some play-action shots for Tyler Shough. The Saints just have too many quality pass catchers for the Panthers, and it'll show. On defense, New Orleans has always had great success against Bryce Young. That'll continue on Sunday, with Chase Young and Carl Granderson harassing Bryce all day and hopefully a rebound performance from the New Orleans secondary. The Panthers could have some success on the ground with Chuba Hubbard, but they won't be able to keep pace with the New Orleans offense. Bold prediction: Tyler Shough gets his first 300-yard passing game since opening week, as both Chris Olave and rookie Jordyn Tyson have over 100 receiving yards. -- Bob Rose Panthers 27, Saints 20 The Saints struggle to sustain drives and Olave's big afternoon isn't enough to overcome missed opportunities. Bryce Young makes enough plays to keep Carolina ahead, forcing New Orleans to play catch-up in the second half. The Panthers get a late defensive stop to seal the win and leave the Saints searching for their first stretch of consecutive wins this season. Bold prediction: Chris Olave eclipses 150 receiving yards despite the loss. -- Arye Pulli Week 2 at Baltimore Ravens, Sunday, Sept. 20, Noon CT (Tommy Gilligan, Tommy Gilligan-USA TODAY Sports) Week 3 vs. Las Vegas Raiders, Sunday, Sept. 27, 3:25 p.m. CT (Chris Graythen, Getty Images) Week 4 vs. Atlanta Falcons, Monday, Oct. 5, 7:15 p.m. CT (Stephen Lew, Stephen Lew-Imagn Images) Week 5 vs. Minnesota Vikings, Sunday, Oct. 11, Noon CT (Chuck Cook, Chuck Cook-USA TODAY Sports) Week 6 at New York Giants, Sunday, Oct. 18, Noon CT (Brad Penner, Brad Penner-Imagn Images) Week 7 vs. Pittsburgh Steelers (in Paris, France), 8:30 a.m. CT (ANDREJ ISAKOVIC, AFP via Getty Images) Week 8 on bye (Stephen Lew, Stephen Lew-USA TODAY Sports) Week 9 vs. Cleveland Browns, Sunday, Nov. 8, Noon CT (Matthew Hinton, Matthew Hinton-Imagn Images) Week 10 vs. Carolina Panthers, Sunday, Nov. 8, Noon CT (Matthew Hinton, Matthew Hinton-Imagn Images) Week 11 at Chicago Bears, Sunday, Nov. 22, Noon CT (David Banks, David Banks-Imagn Images) Week 12 at Cincinnati Bengals, Nov. 29, Noon CT (Aaron Doster, Aaron Doster-USA TODAY Sports) Week 13 vs. Green Bay Packers, Sunday, Dec. 6, Noon CT (Sean Gardner, Getty Images) Week 14 at Carolina Panthers, Sunday, Dec. 13, Noon CT (David Jensen, Getty Images) Week 15 at Tampa Bay Buccaneers, Sunday, Dec. 20, Noon CT (Nathan Ray Seebeck, Nathan Ray Seebeck-Imagn Images) Week 16 vs. Arizona Cardinals, Sunday, Dec. 27, Noon CT (Ella Hall, Getty Images) Week 17 at Atlanta Falcons, Sunday, Jan. 3, Noon CT (Kevin C. away.blurb: New Orleans Saints running back Travis Etienne Jr. has not played since Week 3 due to a hamstring injury, and he's officially listed as questionable for Sunday's game against the Carolina Panthers. The Saints plan to activate RB Travis Etienne Jr. from injured reserve today, putting him in line to return to action Sunday vs. the Panthers, per source. With Etienne in line to return, I'm targeting him in the prop market against a shaky Carolina run defense. Is Travis Etienne Jr. Playing Today? (Injury Update, Betting Impact for Panthers vs. Saints in NFL Week 10) Skip to main content BUY THE ISSUE Etienne is on injured reserve, but it was reported on Saturday that the Saints plan to activate him and play him in Week 10. That's great news for this backfield, as New Orleans is averaging just 3.8 yards per carry as a team and has the fifth-fewest rushing yards in the league through nine weeks. Etienne entered the season as a potential bellcow in this offense after the Saints signed him away from the Jacksonville Jaguars in free agency. Over the first three weeks, Etienne played 50.9 percent of the team's offensive snaps, carrying the ball 30 times for 128 yards (4.3 yards per carry) while also adding 11 catches for 51 yards. He should step into a prominent role in Week 10, as veteran Alvin Kamara is clearly more equipped to handle a change-of-pace role at this stage in his career. Best Travis Etienne Jr. Prop Bet vs. Panthers in NFL Week 10 Travis Etienne Jr. Anytime TD (+115) I'm shying away from any attempts or yardage props for Etienne, ans it's unclear how the Saints will use him in a crowded backfield. Alvin Kamar, Audric Estime and others have handled the workload in recent weeks, and while Etienne could walk into a bellcow role, the team may want to ease him in after he dealt with a soft-tissue injury. So, instead, I'm going to take him to find the end zone against a weak Carolina run defense. This season, the Panthers are allowing 4.6 yards per carry, and they've given up a league-high 13 rushing touchdowns. Etienne should be involved as both a rusher and a receiver, although he didn't find the end zone in his first three games this season. away.headline: Panthers injury report is full of reinforcements
away.blurb: The Carolina Panthers are flailing as they try to stay afloat at the top of the ever pitiful NFC South. The team has dropped three straight games with a skeleton crew of a secondary and a revolving door of players on the offensive line. The first injury report of Week 10 brings good news though. It looks like a lot of key players are soon to return. The highlight of this injury report is all of the full participation from guys that have been out for extended periods of time. Mike Jackson, Jonathon Brooks, and Xavier Legette all had their practice windows opened on Wednesday. That doesn't guarantee that they'll be active on Sunday, but it does mean they need to be activated within the next three weeks. And the fact that they all practiced in full would suggest they're all very close to getting back to live game action. The Saints are very banged up along their offensive line. Starting center Erik McCoy is out. Both starters to his left and the backup left tackle are all dealing with their own injuries, though it doesn't seem like any will miss the game this weekend. Running back Travis Etienne is back at practice, but I wouldn't be surprised if he misses the game even after a limited practice since teams tend to be very cautious with muscle injuries like that. away.headline: Panthers Injury Report & Transactions - Week 10
away.blurb: Offensive lineman Brady Christensen nearly returned from injury last week, but was held out to ensure he was fully ready to go. Hopefully this is the week the versatile player can help plug one of the many, many holes on the Panthers offensive line. He’s currently listed as questionable for Sunday. Speaking of the Panthers offensive line, guard Damien Lewis was a full participant in practice on both Wednesday and Friday, though he was limited on Thursday. The incumbent starter has missed the Panthers last two games. He looks good to go Sunday. The Panthers have three additional questionable players this week in outside linebacker Jaelan Phillips, cornerback Will Lee, and wide receiver Xavier Legette. Carolina could definitely use all three of them, at least situationally. Both cornerback Mike Jackson and running back Jonathon Brooks are doubtful, while linebacker Bobby Okereke is out. Cam Horsley joined the Tennessee Titans last year as an undrafted rookie free agent out of Boston College. To his credit, he made the 53-man roster and appeared in one game, playing 14 defensive snaps without recording any stats. Horsley is a diamond in the rough the Panthers will look to polish to provide some additional depth along the defensive interior. The Panthers are down, but not out. home.headline: Saints Face Offensive Line Injuries Entering Week 10
home.blurb: Finally, coming out of the bye, the New Orleans Saints ' injury issues were getting better, and the team was set to get some very important returns. WR Jordyn Tyson made his first career start, and LT Kelvin Banks Jr. returned against the Cleveland Browns. Both players made massive impacts on the Saints offense and were an important reason why the Saints were able to win that game. New Orleans is also soon getting RB Travis Etienne back, completing the offense and making it fully healthy for the first time this season. Well, until recently. Just when pieces were on their way back, the Saints have lost their starting right tackle and center. Taliese Fuaga popped onto the injury report this week and has been unable to practice since. Being out of Friday's practice meant he was likely going to miss Sunday's important game against the Carolina Panthers, and that's exactly what ended up happening. Then, for McCoy, he was injured near the end of the Browns game. We knew right away that he would be out for a good amount of time. The Saints also ruled out CJ Donaldson and Christen Miller. The offensive line has had a number of issues throughout this season, including some injuries, but this is the worst it's been. Cesar Ruiz will fill in at center, Jeremiah Wright at guard, and likely Asim Richards at RT. Some movements across the offensive line could actually bring some success if it works out, but it's more likely mistakes will arise that really hurt the Saints' offense. The good news is we will finally get some answers about the future. Ruiz is out of contract soon, and so is McCoy. With the veteran center's injuries, the Saints will need to figure out a plan for his replacement, and Ruiz could be that if he does well. Before the NFL, Ruiz only played center in his career, so that's the position he us is more of a natural at. Then, at RG, we get to see more Wright snaps, which could result in him proving he should be the starter next season. Even when this matchup against the Panthers is actually in the Saints' favor, these new injuries could change that.

home.headline: Saints could be on their third-string right tackle against the Bears
home.blurb: We’re about to see the outlook for the New Orleans Saints offensive line go from bad to worse. On Monday, head coach Kellen Moore told reporters that the knee injury Asim Richards suffered in Sunday’s loss to the Carolina Panthers would knock him out for multiple games. The Saints are about to embark on a two-week road trip for matchups with the playoff-ready Chicago Bears and Cincinnati Bengals , and they might be working with their third-string right tackle. Richards was filling in for Taliese Fuaga on the right side, who went down in practice last week with his own knee injury. If Fuaga still can’t play against Chicago this week, the Saints would likely be starting Mason Murphy, who they claimed off of waivers earlier this summer. Richards had drawn a lot of ire from Saints fans for his mistakes in pass protection (he spent most of the last two months replacing Kelvin Banks Jr. at left tackle) but Moore set him up for failure. Richards was given even less help from blocking tight ends and chipping running backs than the starters he replaced, and Moore’s refusal to adjust put him in a bad spot. When asked if Fuaga and center Erik McCoy (who also missed the Panthers game, with a biceps injury) could play this week, Moore offered a noncommittal “We’ll see.” Stay tuned. According to Jets head coach Aaron Glenn, Wilson needs to clear one more step to get out of the consussion protocol, but Glenn believes that will happen in time for Sunday's game. Last week, New York scored just 12 points with Wilson out of the lineup, and it slipped to 16th in the league in EPA/Play on offense as a result. This season, Wilson has appeared in eight of the Jets' nine games, catching 43 passes for 527 yards and three scores. home.headline: Geno Smith's Injury Puts Cade Klubnik's Week 11 Role in Spotlight for New York Jets
home.blurb: The New York Jets have an immediate quarterback question after quarterback Geno Smith (ankle) exited Sunday’s 31-12 loss to the Buffalo Bills. After leaving late in the first half, Smith departed again after one second-half series. The Jets said his availability for Week 11 will be determined during the week. That makes rookie quarterback Cade Klubnik’s relief appearance more than a footnote in another lopsided loss. The fourth-round pick got his first NFL action without the benefit of a week built around his practice reps, then showed both the mobility that can change a possession and the decision-making gaps that come with a sudden assignment. Klubnik finished 11-of-20 for 137 yards and an interception after taking over to open the second half. He led a 10-play, 61-yard drive that ended in a field goal, completing a 28-yard pass to New York Jets wide receiver Garrett Wilson and adding runs of 8 and 12 yards. Smith completed 13 of 21 passes for 148 yards before his exit. Locked On Jets host John Butchko said the circumstances made the rookie’s performance difficult to judge cleanly. He pointed to Klubnik’s ability to create outside the pocket and move the offense early, while also noting risky red-zone throws, an interception and avoidable hits as evidence the rookie is “very much a work in progress.” Butchko said Smith still executes the routine parts of the position more consistently, even if Klubnik brings greater mobility. That distinction matters if Smith cannot practice fully before the trip to Los Angeles. A week of first-team work would give Klubnik more timing with the receivers and a game plan tailored to him, but it would not erase the protection and processing issues exposed by Buffalo’s front. The quarterback uncertainty arrives as the Jets fall to 2-8. Butchko said the loss felt familiar because New York matched Buffalo with 19 first downs and trailed by just 13 yards in total offense, 389-376, yet still lost by 19 points. His larger criticism was that the Jets have repeatedly failed to make timely plays on either side of the ball when a competitive game starts to turn. The Jets visit the Los Angeles Chargers on Nov. 22. Smith’s practice status will determine whether Klubnik remains the backup or gets a full week to prepare for a possible first start. home.headline: Brock Bowers’ ankle injury shows Las Vegas Raiders’ playmaker gap
home.blurb: The Las Vegas Raiders’ 21-13 loss to the Seattle Seahawks in Week 10 showed how little margin their offense has without tight end Brock Bowers. Bowers briefly returned after hurting his ankle on the opening drive but was ruled out at the start of the second half. In his first NFL start, rookie quarterback Fernando Mendoza lost the reliable target who had helped fuel the offense’s early touchdown and field goal. That problem does not diminish the positive parts of Mendoza’s debut. He led a scripted opening touchdown drive with his legs, completed 11 of 13 passes before halftime and did not look overwhelmed against a unit that entered the week ranked first in the NFL in total defense. But the second-half drop-off also illustrated the roster issue around him: The Raiders do not have another dependable top option when Bowers is out. Mendoza finished his first NFL start 17 of 29 for 143 yards, ran for a touchdown and avoided a turnover, but Seattle sacked him six times. The Raiders managed only a field goal after halftime as Mendoza completed 6 of 16 passes for 53 yards; 38 of those yards came on a catch-and-run by running back Ashton Jeanty. Locked On Raiders host Qiant Myers argued that Bowers’ absence allowed Seattle to change the terms of the game. With no other receiver consistently getting separation, Myers said, the Seahawks could commit more resources to pressuring Mendoza and force the first-time starter into checkdowns, scrambles and rushed throws. The protection compounded that problem. Myers said the offensive line left Mendoza exposed to free rushers and argued that Klint Kubiak’s commitment to the run was partly an effort to avoid dropping the rookie back too often behind struggling protection. Mendoza’s mobility prevented additional sacks, but it also became a necessity rather than an added dimension. Bowers is the club’s leading receiving threat, while Jeanty and wide receiver Tre Tucker have supplied complementary production. The injury underscored why adding a true outside playmaker remains central to the rebuild, whether that answer comes through the draft or free agency. Mendoza showed enough composure to support the Raiders’ long-term quarterback plan; Sunday also showed how much help that plan still requires. The Raiders next travel to face the Denver Broncos in Week 11 before a Nov. 29 road game against the Cleveland Browns and their Week 13 bye. Bowers’ availability and Mendoza’s protection will shape how much the offense can ask of its rookie quarterback over that stretch. – Myers questioned the defense after Seattle pulled away in the second half. Seattle wide receiver Jaxon Smith-Njigba found more room after halftime, and Myers pointed to communication issues and unfavorable matchups as recurring problems for the Raiders’ secondary. – The rushing attack again failed to create a dependable counterpunch. The Rams are missing their top two wide receivers, and the Cardinals will be without their starting quarterback, running back, and No. 1 receiver. The Cardinals pulled off one of the biggest upsets of the season in Week 6 when they beat the Rams 18-16. Can they do the same again this Sunday? You can find my best bet for this game in this week's edition of the Road to 272 Bets. In this article, we're going to dive into three of my favorite player props. Rams vs. Cardinals Best NFL Prop Bets Odds via FanDuel Sportsbook Tyler Allgeier 3+ Receptions (+104) Carson Beck OVER 175.5 Passing Yards (-114) Konata Mumpfield Anytime Touchdown (+310) In the Week 10 edition of the Player Prop Countdown , I ranked Tyler Allgeier to haul in three or more receptions as my No. 3 prop bet: Carson Beck will be making his first NFL start on Sunday, and with Michael Wilson now out for the season, I expect him to stick to throwing short routes and screens to the likes of Trey McBride and Tyler Allgeier. Allgeier has already hauled in 23 receptions this season, so with him being the only healthy running back left, I expect that number to continue to tick up in Beck's first start. I'm going to choose to believe in Carson Beck. He had a fantastic season in his senior season at Miami, and he impressed me in this year's preseason. Sure, he may not have the team's best receiver this week, but the Cardinals are likely to play from behind, forcing him into passing situations late in the game. With his total set at just 175.5 yards, I could envision garbage-time yards being enough to get him over the total. With both Puka Nacua and Davante Adams sidelined with injuries, someone has to catch Matthew Stafford's balls out at wide receiver. Konata Mumpfield is the most likely candidate to see the biggest increase in targets. He has 11 receptions for 162 yards and a touchdown already this season, so at odds of north of 3- 1 to score against this bad Cardinals secondary, I'll take that bet without hesitation. Beck will use Allgeier as a safety blanket against this big bad Rams pass rush and we'll see some designed passes to the RB early on, in an attempt to get the rookie comfortable with a couple easy completions. Week 10 picks: Experts predict Rams won't get upset by Cardinals again
picks.blurb: Week 10 picks: Experts predict Rams won't get upset by Cardinals again - Yahoo Sports Search Query for Search Search Home News Finance Sports More Mail NFL Power Rankings Fantasy Football NFL Power Rankings Week 11 Waiver Wire Chargers get first win College football Top 25 Latest NFL updates Week 10 picks: Experts predict Rams won't get upset by Cardinals again Oliver G., Rams Wire · Rams Wire Fri, November 13, 2026 at 1:52 PM UTC · 2 min read Advertisement Advertisement About Our Ads College Sports Sports Business Women's Sports College & High School Adventure Sports What & How To Watch Responsible Gaming Share Your Feedback About Our Ads The Los Angeles Rams head into Week 10 battered and bruised , but with a winning record for the first time all season. They'll also take on an Arizona Cardinals team that upset them in Week 6. A win would help the Rams keep pace for the Wild Card as well as deliver the team's first divisional win in 2026. It'll be an interesting showdown given how well the Rams defense performed in Week 9 with Aaron Donald and Myles Garrett finally on the field together, especially given they'll take on rookie quarterback Carson Beck and a similarly-injured Cardinals offense. Arizona is also without running back Jeremiyah Love and receiver Michael Wilson. The Rams, meanwhile, won't have Puka Nacua, Davante Adams or Jordan Whittington in this game. NFL experts are not expecting an upset this time around. Los Angeles received all 52 picks across seven major outlets, with no analyst picking the Cardinals.
