picks.blurb: NFL expert picks: Dueling predictions for Rams vs. Cardinals - Yahoo Sports Search Query for Search Search Home News Finance Sports More Mail NFL Power Rankings Fantasy Football NFL Power Rankings Week 11 Waiver Wire Chargers get first win College football Top 25 Latest NFL updates NFL expert picks: Dueling predictions for Rams vs. Cardinals Jess Root, Cardinals Wire · Cardinals Wire Sun, November 15, 2026 at 7:24 PM UTC · 1 min read Advertisement Advertisement About Our Ads College Sports Sports Business Women's Sports College & High School Adventure Sports What & How To Watch Responsible Gaming Share Your Feedback About Our Ads The Arizona Cardinals and Los Angeles Rams play Sunday in Week 10. It is the second time they meet. The Cardinals beat the Rams 18-16 at SoFi Stadium in Week 6 on a last-second field goal, as the Cardinals had perhaps their best defensive performance since Nick Rallis became defensive coordinator. This time, both teams have completely different receiving corps, as Michael Wilson, Kendrick Bourne, Davante Adams and Puka Nacua are all on injured reserve. Carson Beck makes his NFL debut but has a backup left tackle and a third-string center protecting him. How will this game play out? We have dueling predictions from the lead writers from Cards Wire and Rams Wire Jess Root, Cards Wire This is going to be a rough game. It is tough seeing the Cardinals being able to do much offensively against the Rams defense. Beck is harassed but shows some promise. The defense gives up a couple of big plays in the run game. Rams 24, Cardinals 13 Cam DaSilve, Rams Wire I'd be more hesitant to pick the Rams if it wasn't a rookie quarterback making his first career start. Rookie QBs are 2-9 all-time against the Rams under McVay, so Carson Beck has his work cut out for him. The Rams' defense will do enough to limit Arizona's offense, and as long as Los Angeles can run the ball, it should be able to maintain possession. Rams 20, Cardinals 10. away.headline: Rams Week 10 injury report vs. Cardinals: Puka Nacua is on IR, so who will step up for LA?
away.blurb: Tyler Higbee stands out as the main weapon to build around in Nacua's absence, particularly on intermediate routes and crucial possession downs. His experience with Stafford makes him a logical candidate for additional attention, although that projection should not be mistaken for an announced target distribution. Higbee's own health briefly complicated that outlook. An illness kept him out Thursday before he returned for limited work Friday. He received no game designation, leaving him available for an offense that needs dependable receiving options. The tight end group's other injuries make his role especially important. Terrance Ferguson is out with ankle and hamstring injuries, while Davis Allen is questionable with an oblique issue. Colby Parkinson offers another available option after progressing to full participation Friday despite injured ribs. Tutu Atwell can provide a different dimension outside. His ability to threaten downfield offers a way to discourage Arizona from crowding shorter routes. Stafford connected with him for a 40-yard gain against the Chargers in Week 8, demonstrating the explosive element available beyond the depleted starting group. CJ Daniels Jr., Xavier Smith and newly promoted Brennan Presley round out the available receiver group. The Rams placed Nacua on IR Thursday to create the roster opening for Presley; Nacua must miss at least four games, making this adjustment more than a one-week assignment. Beyond Nacua's absence, Steve Avila is ruled out after missing every practice with a hamstring injury. Losing an offensive lineman adds another complication as the Rams reshape their passing attack, especially if Stafford needs extra time for unfamiliar combinations to develop. Allen's questionable designation follows limited practices Wednesday and Friday around a missed Thursday session. Long snapper Joe Cardona is also questionable after remaining limited throughout the week with an ankle injury. Defensively, Myles Garrett carries a questionable designation for a knee issue and rest. He was limited Wednesday and Thursday before sitting out Friday. His availability matters after a three-sack performance against Washington helped Los Angeles secure its third consecutive victory. Trent McDuffie and Kam Curl are questionable, too. Both returned for limited work Friday after two missed sessions, managing back and toe injuries, respectively. Braden Fiske missed Friday with an ankle injury but received no game designation. Byron Young and Aaron Donald also sat out for rest without designations, distinguishing their absences from confirmed injury-related setbacks. home.headline: NFL injury news: Cardinals QB Gardner Minshew suffers torn UCL, set for season ending surgery | Report
home.source: The Sunday Guardian Live on MSN
home.blurb: India, Nov. 15 -- Arizona Cardinals quarterback Gardner Minshew is set to undergo season-ending surgery after suffering a torn ulnar collateral ligament (UCL) in his throwing elbow. ESPN NFL insider Adam Schefter reported on November 15 that Minshew is planning to have the surgery, although he is still working on the timing of the procedure. The injury is a major setback for the Cardinals, who have already placed the veteran quarterback on Injured Reserve. Minshew's 2026 campaign is officially over, leaving rookie Carson Beck to take charge of Arizona's quarterback room. Gardner Minshew To Undergo Surgery After Torn UCL Injury According to Schefter, Minshew is expected to undergo surgery to address the torn UCL in his right elbow. While the quarterback has not finalised when he will have the procedure, he is planning to go ahead with the operation. The injury occurred during Arizona's Week 9 matchup against the Seattle Seahawks on November 8. Seahawks linebacker Dante Fowler Jr. hit Minshew during his throwing motion on the final play of the first half, forcing a fumble. Minshew immediately appeared to be in discomfort but surprisingly returned after halftime and completed the game. He finished the contest with 21 completions on 30 attempts for 166 passing yards. However, the Cardinals suffered a 17-3 defeat against Seattle. Cardinals Place Gardner Minshew On Injured Reserve The Arizona Cardinals officially placed Minshew on Injured Reserve on November 10, confirming that he would miss the remainder of the 2026 season. Before suffering the injury, Minshew had completed 38 of 53 passes for 354 yards and three touchdowns across two appearances for Arizona. His brief stint with the Cardinals included an impressive performance against the Dallas Cowboys in Week 8. Coming off the bench, Minshew threw for 188 yards and three touchdowns, helping Arizona secure a dramatic 33-30 overtime victory. His performance earned him the starting quarterback position, but his promotion was followed by the devastating elbow injury. Carson Beck Takes Over As Cardinals Starting Quarterback With Minshew sidelined, rookie quarterback Carson Beck is expected to lead the Cardinals' offence. Arizona has also strengthened its quarterback depth by signing veteran Josh Johnson and rookie Joey Aguilar. Johnson joined from the Cincinnati Bengals' practice squad, while Aguilar arrived from the Jacksonville Jaguars' practice squad. The Cardinals are now relying on their rookie quarterback to navigate the remainder of a challenging season. Minshew's injury also creates uncertainty surrounding his future in Arizona, as the veteran quarterback is scheduled to become a free agent after the 2026 campaign. For now, the priority will be his recovery following surgery as the Cardinals look to move forward without their experienced signal caller.

home.headline: Rams Week 10 injury report vs. Cardinals: Puka Nacua is on IR, so who will step up for LA?
home.blurb: Tyler Higbee stands out as the main weapon to build around in Nacua's absence, particularly on intermediate routes and crucial possession downs. His experience with Stafford makes him a logical candidate for additional attention, although that projection should not be mistaken for an announced target distribution. Higbee's own health briefly complicated that outlook. An illness kept him out Thursday before he returned for limited work Friday. He received no game designation, leaving him available for an offense that needs dependable receiving options. The tight end group's other injuries make his role especially important. Terrance Ferguson is out with ankle and hamstring injuries, while Davis Allen is questionable with an oblique issue. Colby Parkinson offers another available option after progressing to full participation Friday despite injured ribs. Tutu Atwell can provide a different dimension outside. His ability to threaten downfield offers a way to discourage Arizona from crowding shorter routes. Stafford connected with him for a 40-yard gain against the Chargers in Week 8, demonstrating the explosive element available beyond the depleted starting group. CJ Daniels Jr., Xavier Smith and newly promoted Brennan Presley round out the available receiver group. The Rams placed Nacua on IR Thursday to create the roster opening for Presley; Nacua must miss at least four games, making this adjustment more than a one-week assignment. Beyond Nacua's absence, Steve Avila is ruled out after missing every practice with a hamstring injury. Losing an offensive lineman adds another complication as the Rams reshape their passing attack, especially if Stafford needs extra time for unfamiliar combinations to develop. Allen's questionable designation follows limited practices Wednesday and Friday around a missed Thursday session. Long snapper Joe Cardona is also questionable after remaining limited throughout the week with an ankle injury. Defensively, Myles Garrett carries a questionable designation for a knee issue and rest. He was limited Wednesday and Thursday before sitting out Friday. His availability matters after a three-sack performance against Washington helped Los Angeles secure its third consecutive victory. Trent McDuffie and Kam Curl are questionable, too. Both returned for limited work Friday after two missed sessions, managing back and toe injuries, respectively. Braden Fiske missed Friday with an ankle injury but received no game designation. Byron Young and Aaron Donald also sat out for rest without designations, distinguishing their absences from confirmed injury-related setbacks. picks.blurb: Cowboys vs 49ers: Final score predictions for Week 10 - Yahoo Sports Search Query for Search Search Home News Finance Sports More Mail NFL Power Rankings Fantasy Football NFL Power Rankings Week 11 Waiver Wire Chargers get first win College football Top 25 Latest NFL updates Cowboys vs 49ers: Final score predictions for Week 10 Photo by Michael Zagaris/San Francisco 49ers/Getty Images | Getty Images Mike Poland · SB Nation Sun, November 15, 2026 at 7:00 PM UTC · 4 min read Advertisement Advertisement About Our Ads College Sports Sports Business Women's Sports College & High School Adventure Sports What & How To Watch Responsible Gaming Share Your Feedback About Our Ads The Dallas Cowboys return home at 4-5 after escaping the Indianapolis Colts with a nail-biting victory, but the difficulty level rises considerably this week. The San Francisco 49ers are at 7-1 and own the best record in the NFC. Dallas showed against the Colts that its offense can move the football against anybody, but beating San Francisco will require a much cleaner performance, and scoring touchdowns rather than settling for field goals, or worse, falling victim to turnovers. When San Francisco has the ball Everything starts with Christian McCaffrey. San Francisco does not need him to simply line up and run between the tackles, Kyle Shanahan moves him around, gets him involved in the passing game and uses his presence to create space for everyone else. McCaffrey already has nine rushing touchdowns, while Brock Purdy has thrown 17 touchdowns against only five interceptions and ranks among the NFL's most efficient quarterbacks. San Francisco also leads the league in red-zone touchdown rate at an incredible 84%, so Dallas cannot rely on tightening up once the 49ers get close to the goal line. When Dallas has the ball Dallas should take confidence from what it produced in Indianapolis. The Cowboys gained 508 total yards, with Dak Prescott throwing for 335, CeeDee Lamb producing 195 receiving yards and Javonte Williams topping 100 yards rushing. The problem was everything around those numbers. Dallas committed 14 penalties and lost two fumbles, turning what should have been a comfortable win into another game that required Prescott to rescue them in the final minutes. The good news is San Francisco's defense can be attacked. Despite all the talent in its front seven, the 49ers have only 15 sacks, ranking 28th in the NFL. Nick Bosa and recently acquired DeForest Buckner make the defensive line much more dangerous than that number suggests, but Dallas should still give Prescott opportunities to attack downfield. Lamb is now up to 904 receiving yards and is coming off one of his best games of the season. San Francisco also began the week with injuries to their starting cornerbacks and their game status is questionable. If either is missing or limited, Lamb becomes the obvious place for Dallas to attack. Now onto the predictions from your BTB writers… Tom Ryle (4-5) I just don't see the Cowboys being that competitive against one of the Super Bowl favorites. In a matchup of organizational dysfunction and well oiled machine, I'll sadly pick the 49ers to win 31-16. Brandon Loree (6-3) At this point, it's probably the Cowboys' toughest challenge and, unfortunately, their biggest thorn in the side since 2021. The 49ers are way better in almost every category compared to Dallas despite having similar if not worse, injury luck. If the Cowboys can somehow pull a rabbit out of their hat and win this game, get ready to hear some outrageous playoff talk. Seeing is believing, so I'll have to see it happen in order to believe—Dallas loses at home 33-23. Dyllan Rivers (5-4) Sometimes the NFL makes absolutely no sense. Teams that have no business winning will go out and upset the heavy favorite. But this is not one of those weeks. Christian McCaffrey goes crazy and Dallas falls to the 49ers 37-27. Matt Holleran (4-5) Until I see it happen I refuse to believe the Cowboys will beat a Kyle Shanahan-lead 49ers team. Dallas does not win back-to-back games under Brian Schottenheimer and I would be absolutely shocked if they did just that against a San Francisco team that just may be the best in the league. I hope I'm wrong, but I don't see this one being close. Give me the 49ers in a rout, 37-17. Mike Poland (4-5) An entire panel going for the 49ers to win this one, and my head says the Cowboys lose this week to a strong San Francisco roster. But I'll break the clean sweep here so any optimistic Cowboys fans here on BTB have something to align with on the staff predictions. A very tentative and nervous score prediction here where Dallas wins 28-21. And I'm willing to take the hit on this one. Put your prediction in the comments before the game begins.

picks.blurb: 49ers vs. Cowboys bold predictions for NFL Week 10 - Yahoo Sports Search Query for Search Search Home News Finance Sports More Mail NFL Power Rankings Fantasy Football NFL Power Rankings Week 11 Waiver Wire Chargers get first win College football Top 25 Latest NFL updates 49ers vs. Cowboys bold predictions for NFL Week 10 Douglas Fritz, ClutchPoints · ClutchPoints Tue, November 10, 2026 at 11:03 PM UTC · 5 min read Advertisement Advertisement About Our Ads College Sports Sports Business Women's Sports College & High School Adventure Sports What & How To Watch Responsible Gaming Share Your Feedback About Our Ads While the San Francisco 49ers made a fairly mild move, the Dallas Cowboys didn't move the needle at the trade deadline. But these teams meet in Week 10 of the NFL season, and here are bold predictions for the contest. Entering with a record of 7-1, the 49ers sit as the No. 1 in the NFC. Meanwhile, the Cowboys are trying to fight their way back into contention in the NFC East. They have a record of 4-5. The 49ers are road favorites, but only by 3.5 points. Watch sports LIVE with fuboTV (free trial) 49ers QB Brock Purdy will throw for 250 yards and two TD passes It's a matter of scheme that Purdy will have success , according to ESPN. "Kyle Shanahan will have answers for both the run and pass game Sunday in Dallas," Matt Bowen wrote. "Schemed throws for Brock Purdy that create open coverage voids off play-action, plus a multiple run game with Christian McCaffrey and Kaelon Black to attack a Cowboys defense, allowing 5.0 YPC (third most). I like the 49ers to cover on the road." Purdy has thrown for 1,980 yards this season with 17 touchdowns and five interceptions. He has been impressive and has the eye of head coach Kyle Shanahan, according to a post on X by 95.7 TheGame via Heavy.com. "Yeah, it's been amazing," Shanahan said. "Just since the first game he got in there. That's why I struggle at the beginning of the year when everyone's asking me, can I believe how good he's playing and how much better he's improved because he was so good off the bench versus Miami in his first game and the second week… taking us to the NFC Championship as a rookie. "And I think his second year took us to the Super Bowl maybe. So Brock's been the man since he's come in, and it's pretty unbelievable deal considering where he was drafted, how he started… very fortunate to have Brock." The Cowboys will have their hands full. Cowboys WR CeeDee Lamb will get 8-plus catches and 90-plus yards The Cowboys are going to get the ball to Lamb. It's their best path to having a shot at beating the 49ers. Lamb left the win over the Colts with a sigh of relief, according to dallascowboys.com. "Those are the games that you love to end up on top," Lamb said. "We understand it was the same situation that we were kind of in last week, and we didn't end up on top then, so just finishing out the game, finishing out the drive — shout out to the defense for ending the game. "But I think I had, like, three penalties alone in the second half, and a fumble. Personally, I gotta take a real good look. The numbers look crazy, but it could have been more. And I'm always thinking about what could have been. So, as for me, as a leader on this offense,I feel like I've got to be better in some realms and just end the game." The 49ers are off to a great start. But before the season, the Cowboys were in the same conversation with them. Lamb said the Cowboys need to get the job done. "We know what we got going on, just the history of that [matchup], the guys that they have over there on defense and the prep, I mean, it's going to take a lot of a lot of preparation, and a lot of execution," Lamb said. "We can't have as many flags because they have a really good offense, too." Prescott will lean heavily on Lamb if George Pickens misses another game. But even if Pickens plays, Prescott won't forget who he needs to target, early and often. 49ers RB Christian McCaffrey will get in the end zone twice Look for McCaffrey to score on the ground and with a reception. The 49ers are going to get him the ball near the goal line. One thing that helps McCaffrey's overall usage is that Shanahan is more confident that he is ready to rock after a pre-bye injury slowed him somewhat, according to ninerswire.com. "No. I actually forgot about it," Shanahan said. "He had a good bye week, and he told me before the bye week in Christian style not to worry about it at all. He'll be fine, and he looked good all week." McCaffrey hasn't had a blowout game all season. His rushing high is 75 yards, and his receiving high is 61. But he has 10 total touchdowns, with nine of them coming off the ground. And consistency has been a hallmark. McCaffrey has scored in seven straight games. In three of those contests, he scored twice. The 49ers will need to be sharp offensively. Despite the way their defense has played, they will have trouble slowing down the Cowboys' high-octane offense. McCaffrey will likely need those scores to keep his team in good business. away.headline: 49ers fans push back after Adam Thielen says he won't sign with San Francisco: 'That ship has sailed'
away.blurb: The San Francisco 49ers have enjoyed an incredible season so far, with their only setback coming in an out-of-the-blue 29-20 loss to the Atlanta Falcons. They hold an 8-1 record and have bounced back from that loss by securing two wins on the bounce. In an interview with KFAN1003, Thielen spoke on his physical condition and potential return to the NFL, insisting that he remains in good enough shape to compete despite being away from regular game action. “My workout room is right next to me right here, and I was working out before I got on the show this morning,” Thielen said. “So, I play basketball twice a week, so I’m probably in better shape than I was when I was playing. I’m always ready, man… I’m in good shape. I’m ready.” Despite their strong performance, San Francisco has faced several challenges throughout the season. Bringing in an experienced wide receiver could give their mighty offense an additional boost. Former All-Pro wide receiver Adam Thielen was asked if he’d consider alleviating the Niners’ injury problems and making a comeback, a possibility he shot down nearly instantly. Niners Fans Fire Back at Adam Thielen On whether he would answer the phone if an NFL team comes calling, he replied: “Oh, 100%.” Then, when a host asked him if signing with the Niners was something he’d consider, he made his stance crystal clear: “I’m not going to the 49ers.” It didn’t take long for 49ers fans to take notice of his comments. IMPROVE YOUR TEAM: PFN’s Free Fantasy Trade Calculator “Sorry, no room on the practice squad at this time,” one Niners fan wrote in response . “Good, we wouldn’t want him,” another said . Thielen enjoyed a respectable NFL career after entering the league as an undrafted free agent in 2013. He established himself as a dependable wide receiver and became one of the Minnesota Vikings’ most consistent offensive contributors. He earned two Pro Bowl selections and recorded multiple 1,000-yard receiving seasons. Thielen has also played for the Carolina Panthers and spent time with the Pittsburgh Steelers. In the 2025 season with the Steelers, he made five appearances and three starts for Pittsburgh, recording 11 receptions for 117 yards. PREDICT THE NFL SEASON: PFN’s Free NFL Playoff Predictor Thielen’s experience could make him an interesting option for a team seeking depth. But his latest comments suggest that San Francisco, which ranks No. 2 in PFN Offense Impact with an 88.9 grade, will not be among his preferred destinations. Meanwhile, some fans questioned whether the 49ers would have any interest in bringing him aboard in the first place. “Bro thinks the Niners would call him,” a fan wrote . “Jesus Thielen, give it up! That ship has sailed!” one said . “I’d rather see OBJ back than Adam Thielen EVER again,” one added . Thielen announced his retirement from the NFL in January. The Niners, meanwhile, will be back in action in Week 11 when they take on the Vikings in Mexico City. This article originally appeared on Pro Footba

home.headline: Cowboys Reportedly Sign New RB After 2026 NFL Trade Deadline, Tyler Goodson Injury
home.blurb: The TCU product was available because the New Orleans Saints released him after he appeared in six games for the NFC South team this season. He ran for 159 yards and two touchdowns on an ugly 2.8 yards per carry in those six games. Dallas Cowboys fans may have been hoping for a more consequential move ahead of Tuesday's 4 p.m. ET NFL trade deadline, but they reportedly did make a running back addition. Calvin Watkins of the Dallas Morning News reported the Cowboys signed Kendre Miller to its practice squad with Tyler Goodson dealing with a knee injury he suffered in Sunday's win over the Indianapolis Colts. Head coach Brian Schottenheimer told reporters Monday that Goodson will miss "multiple weeks" with the setback. The timing was less than ideal for Goodson, as he was just starting to establish himself in the running back rotation behind Javonte Williams. He finished with a season-high 12 carries for 77 yards in the win over the Colts, which marked his second time in a three-game span with double-digit carries. Yet his injury put the team in scramble mode as it attempted to find another backup for Williams. Enter Miller, whom ESPN's Todd Archer reported visited with the Cowboys on Tuesday before their decision to sign him. Miller was also an occasional threat in the Saints' passing game with nine catches on a career-high 13 targets this season. While he isn't someone who is going to carry the offense on his back, the Cowboys won't ask him to do so. Instead, he will surely be put in a role where he is expected to fill in for Williams on a handful of series throughout games to keep the starter fresher for the stretch run. Next up for Dallas is a home game against the San Francisco 49ers.

Plus, how to watch, what to know, and a prediction Getty Images The 10th Sunday of the 2026 NFL regular season will conclude with the Pittsburgh Steelers and Cincinnati Bengals battling for first place in the AFC North division. Pittsburgh (6-2) currently leads the North by virtue of its Week 5 win over Cincinnati (6-2). The Steelers have won seven of the last nine games between the two teams dating back to the start of the 2022 season. The second of those two losses occurred the last time these two teams played in Cincinnati. Last October, Cincinnati won a 33-31 shootout. The Steelers won the rematch a month later in Pittsburgh. Here's how you can follow the action in real time. We've also included a breakdown and a prediction for Sunday night's showdown. Where to watch Bengals vs. Steelers live When: Sunday, Nov. 15 | Time: 8:20 p.m. ET Where: Paycor Stadium -- Cincinnati, Ohio TV: NBC | Stream: fubo (try for free) Follow: CBS Sports App Odds: Bengals -3.5, O/U 47.5 (via DraftKings ) Follow Live: Bengals vs. Steelers live blog with analysis, updates, and more Bengals vs. Steelers: Need to know Last time we met The Steelers sealed a 30-27 win when Derrick Harmon strip-sacked Joe Burrow on the Bengals' final series. Cincinnati was in field goal range when the turnover occurred. Jaylen Warren was the catalyst for Pittsburgh's win. The fifth-year veteran rushed for 127 yards on 17 carries and caught three passes for 49 yards. Warren's success helped open things up for Aaron Rodgers , who threw for 292 yards and three touchdowns with one interception. Rodgers was able to top Burrow, who threw for 282 yards and three touchdowns. Red hot teams Both Pittsburgh and Cincinnati come into this game with four-game winning streaks. The Steelers went into their Week 9 bye with a 27-6 win over the Browns . Cincinnati is coming off a 34-17 win over the Falcons in Madrid, Spain. It'll be interesting to see how much the previous week will impact Sunday night's game. The Bengals may still be feeling the effects of traveling overseas. The Steelers, meanwhile, are rested and might be getting back some key players who have missed time with injuries. One of those players is Harmon, who has missed time with a foot injury. Reasons for success Pittsburgh's success has been powered by Warren (and, to a lesser degree, fellow running back Rico Dowdle , who has played well in a complementary role since returning from his injury in Week 6) and a defense that hasn't allowed a touchdown in seven quarters. Pittsburgh is once again getting high-level play from T.J. Watt , who has already eclipsed his 2025 sack tally. Cincinnati's current winning streak has largely been the byproduct of Burrow (who leads the NFL in completion percentage and touchdown passes) and his success throwing to Ja'Marr Chase and Tee Higgins . The Bengals have also received solid play from a defense that is getting big contributions from offseason acquisitions Dexter Lawrence and Boye Mafe . Prediction, pick This game will come down to two things: Pittsburgh's ability to throw the ball (which would in turn help open things up for the running game) and Cincinnati's ability to keep Burrow clean, which has at times been an issue against the Steelers. The Bengals want to make this a shootout, while the Steelers will want to play keep-away while keeping Burrow and Co. on the sideline. away.headline: Steelers get good injury news on three players for Week 10 vs. Bengals
away.blurb: Courtesy of Wednesday's Week 10 injury report, the Steelers saw three players, who have missed time with their respective injuries, return to practice as full participants: wide receiver Ben Skowronek (calf), cornerback Brandin Echols (hamstring), and cornerback Doneiko Slaughter (hamstring). Steelers get good injury news on three players for Week 10 vs. Bengals - Yahoo Sports Search Query for Search Search Home News Finance Sports More Mail NFL Steelers get good injury news on three players for Week 10 vs. Bengals Andrew Vasquez, Steelers Wire · Steelers Wire Thu, November 12, 2026 at 3:58 PM UTC · 2 min read Advertisement Advertisement About Our Ads The Pittsburgh Steelers received great injury news regarding three of their players ahead of their Week 10 matchup against the Cincinnati Bengal s. Skowronek, who began his career with the Los Angeles Rams (2021–2023), also spent time with the Houston Texans (2024) before joining the Steelers in 2024. A solid wide receiver depth piece and special teams ace, Skowronek suffered his calf injury in Week 5 and has missed the past three games. Echols, who began his career with the New York Jets (2021–2024), joined the Steelers in 2025 free agency. An underrated contributor for Pittsburgh's defense last season, Echols suffered his hamstring injury during Week 6 and has missed the past two games. Slaughter, who began his NFL career with the Jacksonville Jaguars (2025), joined the Steelers on a reserve/future contract in January 2026. After a strong preseason and training camp, Slaughter was signed back to the active roster on October 10, but unfortunately suffered a hamstring injury in Week 7 and has missed the past game. The fact that Skowronek, Echols, and Slaughter were able to be full participants at Wednesday's practice gives them an excellent shot at returning in Week 10 for Sunday Night Football against the Bengals . away.headline: Steelers’ DeShon Elliott Suffers Pregame Injury, Out Against Bengals
away.blurb: Steelers’ DeShon Elliott Suffers Pregame Injury, Out Against Bengals Skip to main content SI.COM According to ESPN's Adam Schefter, safety DeShon Elliott suffered a knee injury during pregame warm-ups at Paycor Stadium and has been ruled out vs. Cincinnati as a result. Steelers S Deshon Elliott injured his knee during the pregame and has been ruled out for tonight’s game vs. Cincinnati. Elliott was listed on the injury report this week with an ankle injury, though he was a full participant on both November 12 and 13 after initially being limited on November 11, and thus was not listed with a game designation. The Pittsburgh Steelers have lost a key piece of their secondary for a monumental Week 10 showdown against the Cincinnati Bengals on Sunday Night Football. Having to face an explosive Bengals passing offense led by quarterback Joe Burrow as well as the star wide receiver duo of Ja'Marr Chase and Tee Higgins now becomes much tougher of a task for Pittsburgh without Elliott on the field. The Steelers, though, were able to at least hold Cincinnati in check to an extent during their first meeting this season, which resulted in a 30-27 victory for the black and gold at Acrisure Stadium in Week 3. Elliott was not active for that contest either, while residing on the reserve/injured list to open the year after going down with a season-ending knee/hamstring injury in Week 8 of the 2025 campaign. home.blurb: Starting right guard Dalton Risner exited Sunday’s game in the middle of the second quarter. He was questionable to play at all with an illness, but has also been dealing with a knee injury for most of the season. Dylan Fairchild’s not out of the woods yet, either Fairchild was able to play the whole game until some of the starters were taken out during garbage time in the fourth quarter. He was day-to-day upon coming back from Madrid, but ended up as a full participant to end the week of practice. This is where rookie Brian Parker II would come in handy. Parker was designated to return off of Injured Reserve late last week , indicating he is very close to being able to play after suffering a knee injury to end the preseason. He played LG quite admirably in the preseason. He may just be their best option at the position in Fairchild can’t go. Cincinnati has been blessed with tremendous continuity along it’s o-line. That continuity was challenged on Sunday night against the Pittsburgh Steelers, and it will be a story to watch over the next seven days as well. The Cincinnati Bengals offensive line has been able to handle all kinds of competition this season. They could be facing their biggest opponent this week, and it’s not the Washington Commanders. Dalton Risner dealing with knee problems Coach Zac Taylor told reporters Monday they would see where Risner was at throughout the week, but also confirmed that he’s dealing with an issue in each of his knees, not just one. “His knees are bothering him,” Taylor said during his weekly Monday presser . “So we’ll get more information on it, see where it’s at.” “Yeah, both his knees started bothering him.” Risner last appeared on the injury report listed with a knee injury in Week 5. He has been playing with a brace ever since. That he’s dealing with problems in both of his knees is a bit concerning going forward. To the left of center Ted Karras, starting left guard Dylan Fairchild is also still battling a pec injury he suffered in Week 9 against the Atlanta Falcons. “Same,” Taylor said of the plan with Fairchild in relation to Risner. “We’ll kind of see where he’s at through the week.” The Cincinnati Bengals have a 98% chance to make the NFL playoffs and an 8% chance to win Super Bowl LXI, according to the A to Z Sports NFL Playoff Predictor (updated Mon, Nov 16). Likely backup plans at both guard spots Risner was replaced by second-year G Jalen River s. Cincinnati selected rivers in the fifth round of the 2025 NFL Draft, and started him in seven games as a rookie last season. It was his knee injury last year that forced Risner onto the field late in the year. Should Risner miss this week, it will likely be Rivers again at RG. The LG spot is a bit more interesting. LogoParamountPlus More live games and exclusives Log Out Connect TV Provider More live games & exclusives Log Out Connect NFL News & Highlights Plus, how to watch, odds, a preview and a prediction for the Monday night matchup Imagn Images In the Week 10 edition of "Monday Night Football," the Baltimore Ravens play host to the Los Angeles Chargers . Baltimore is coming off a disastrous Thursday night loss to the Jacksonville Jaguars , during which the offense looked inept with third-string quarterback Joe Fagnano under center while nursing an injury. The Ravens will now turn to the recently acquired Jacoby Brissett in hopes that he can reinvigorate the attack in the absence of both Lamar Jackson and Tyler Huntley . Los Angeles is in the midst of an epic disaster of a season, having started the year 0-8 and looking horrific on both sides of the ball. The Chargers are once again beset by a cavalcade of injuries, but that is no excuse for just how poorly they have played. They're the only winless team in the league at the moment, so they'll be looking for their first victory of the season. Will the Ravens bounce back, or will the Chargers finally get on the board? We'll find out soon enough. Before we break down the matchup, here's a look at how you can watch the game. Where to watch Ravens vs. Chargers live Date: Monday, Nov. 16 | Time: 8:15 p.m. ET Location: M&T Bank Stadium (Baltimore) TV: ESPN/ABC | Streaming: Fubo ( try for free ) Follow: CBS Sports App Odds: Ravens -4.5, O/U 38.5 via DraftKings Sportsbook When the Chargers have the ball The Chargers are 26th in the NFL in total yards and 32nd (a.k.a., last) in points. They average a mere 4.7 yards per play, which is 29th in the league, and they have scored points on only 27.4% of their drives while turning it over a league-worst 18.9% of the time. They lead the NFL in pre-snap penalties per game. They don't do anything well, and they often put themselves behind the eight ball with inexcusable mistakes. Justin Herbert looks like a broken quarterback, completing just 61.3% of his passes at an average of 6.8 yards per attempt, with six touchdown passes against a league-worst 11 interceptions. His receiver corps has been brutal all season, dropping passes and seemingly miscommunicating with him on routes left and right. He once again won't have Ladd McConkey on Monday evening, either, which will leave the uninspiring trio of Quentin Johnston , Tre Harris and KeAndre Lambert-Smith as his top perimeter options. Los Angeles has been entirely unable to run the ball, with Omarion Hampton , Keaton Mitchell and Kimani Vidal combining for 709 yards on 184 carries -- an average of 3.8 yards per tote. The offensive line has given them no room to run whatsoever, clearing the way for only 0.90 yards before contact per carry, according to Tru Media. The backs themselves have a slightly below-average avoided tackle rate, but they still check in considerably below average in yards after contact per carry. Other than all that, though, things are going really well! That said, the Ravens do provide the Chargers with an opportunity to at least move the ball. Baltimore is 25th in the league in scoring defense and 21st in yards allowed per play. The Ravens have shown themselves to be beatable mostly through the air, as they've allowed only 3.6 yards per carry this season. Herbert doesn't have his top receiving option available in this game, but if the offensive line can actually provide him with adequate time to throw (not a guarantee with this group, obviously), then perhaps he can throw the ball to the guys wearing his color shirts rather than the opposing team for a change. When the Ravens have the ball It's hard to know what to expect from Baltimore's offense given that the Ravens are now on their fourth starting quarterback. This time around, it is the one who has yet to play with his new team and arrived in town just a week and a half ago. We know that Brissett has completed 63.3% of his passes for only 5.6 yards per attempt this season, with 10 touchdowns against seven interceptions. We also know that he was benched in favor of Gardner Minshew before being traded from Arizona to Baltimore. He's competent and can keep the offense moving at times, but he doesn't offer much in terms of ceiling. We also know that Brissett likes to hyper-target his top options in the passing game. We saw that in Arizona with Trey McBride and Michael Wilson , but we also saw it in other stops, like when he honed in on Amari Cooper during his year as the starter with the Cleveland Browns . The Ravens already focus the majority of their passing game on wide receiver Zay Flowers , and it wouldn't be surprising if Brissett peppered him with targets here. Flowers was having a monster season with Lamar Jackson and even Tyler Huntley under center, but he did nothing the last two weeks with Joe Fagnano in the lineup, essentially. He should get back to producing at a decent level here, provided that offensive coordinator Declan Doyle moves him around the formation rather than parking him in the slot, where the Chargers have been better in coverage than they have been on the outside. Still, the Ravens will likely look to center the offense on Derrick Henry , so that Brissett doesn't have to do a ton of heavy lifting. Henry hasn't been as efficient this season (3.9 yards per carry) as he was during his first two years with the Ravens (5.6 per carry), presumably in part because he hasn't had Jackson to draw defensive attention away from his runs up the middle. Henry does still have a 53.7% rushing success rate, but he hasn't broken the types of long runs we've been used to seeing from him because the wider rushing lanes are not available with defenses crowding the box. He's run into an eight-man box on 30.9% of his carries, according to Tru Media, the third-highest rate among the 26 players with at least 100 rushing attempts so far this season. The Chargers have actually been half-way decent against the run this year, allowing 4.1 yards per carry to opposing running backs, but they've been hit for explosives at an above-average rate. If they don't get Henry on the ground quickly, he could hit a crease and take it a long way. If that starts happening, it'll open things up for Brissett to work the play-action game, which could lead to big plays for the likes of Flowers, Ja'Kobi Lane and perhaps even Mark Andrews . I don't feel good at all about predicting the Chargers to actually keep a game close, but that's what I'm going to do here. I'm not going as far as predicting that they'll get their first win, but I think they can hang in the game against Jacoby Brissett in his first start with Baltimore. The Ravens' offense should be better than it was with Joe Fagnano under center, but I'm not sure it will fully hit the ground running right away. LA's offense is pretty broken, but the Ravens haven't exactly been great defensively (25th in scoring defense), so the Chargers might be able to put at least some points on the board. Prediction: Ravens 24, Chargers 20 Now Playing Share Share Video Ravens vs. Chargers: Can LA finally get its first win on 'MNF?' Fortunately, Monday night's matchup against the Baltimore Ravens could be one of their best chances to finally get into the win column. Baltimore is dealing with major injuries, including the absence of Lamar Jackson, and will turn to newly acquired quarterback Jacoby Brissett . The Ravens are also struggling to find consistency at 4-5. Meanwhile, the Chargers are coming off another ugly loss after allowing C.J. Stroud to throw for 384 yards and five touchdowns. Could Jim Harbaugh finally get his team a victory? Here are three bold predictions for Chargers-Ravens on Monday Night Football. Watch sports LIVE with fuboTV (free trial) Bold Prediction No. 3: Jacoby Brissett throws for 2+ touchdowns in Ravens debut Mark J. Rebilas-Imagn Images Brissett is now a Raven, and his first start with Baltimore will come at home against the Chargers . Los Angeles has a solid defense and typically does a good job making life difficult for opposing quarterbacks. However, that certainly wasn't the case against Houston. Stroud walked all over the Chargers on Sunday, throwing for 384 yards and five touchdowns. Brissett isn't the same kind of quarterback, but he has plenty of NFL experience and should have enough weapons around him to make an impact in his first game with Baltimore. I expect at least two of his passes to find the end zone Monday night. Zay Flowers could be in line for a productive performance, which would be welcome news for fantasy managers who have been waiting for the Ravens' offense to get back on track. Bold Prediction No. 2: Keaton Mitchell scores a touchdown against his former team This is probably the boldest prediction of the three. Mitchell will face his former team for the first time since joining the Chargers, and I think he'll find a way to make his return memorable. Mitchell has one touchdown this season, and it came through the air. He's recorded 46 carries for 178 yards, averaging 3.9 yards per attempt, while adding 18 receptions for 103 yards. The Chargers have continued to rotate their running backs, making it difficult to predict which player will receive the most opportunities. However, Mitchell has shown that he can contribute as both a runner and receiver. In primetime, I expect him to get a chance near the goal line and take advantage of it. Scoring against the team that gave him his NFL opportunity would make for a pretty good Monday night story. Bold Prediction No. 1: The Chargers win their first game of the 2026 season The Chargers have a chance to win? Yes, they do. Without Lamar Jackson under center, Baltimore is a much more vulnerable opponent. The Ravens are 4-5, dealing with injuries and trying to get their season back on track. Meanwhile, the Chargers are desperate to avoid falling to 0-9. There's also an interesting storyline on the sideline. Jesse Minter , who previously served as the Chargers' defensive coordinator, will face his former boss, Jim Harbaugh, for the first time as opposing head coaches. Harbaugh's first season in Los Angeles has been a disaster, but this is an opportunity to give his team something positive. Justin Herbert needs to play much better than he did against Houston, and I expect him to respond with a more competitive performance. Baltimore still has plenty of defensive talent. Marlon Humphrey and Roquan Smith could make things difficult for Herbert, while Kyle Hamilton would be another major factor if he's healthy enough to play. This could be an ugly game, with both offenses struggling to find consistency. However, I think the Chargers finally get over the hump and leave Baltimore with a victory. Score Prediction: Chargers win 20-17, with Cameron Dicker making four field goals. Los Angeles can't go 0-17, can it? This is one of its best remaining opportunities to avoid that nightmare, and I'm picking the Chargers to take advantage. Los Angeles has been dealing with injuries all season long, by Week Six they already had over half of their original 53-man roster on the injury report or injured reserve. The Chargers injury luck is not improving much. For all the jokes and talk about the electrical substation near the San Francisco 49ers practice facility, Los Angeles may have something worse. The Chargers' practice facility, the Bolt, is located near Los Angeles International Airport, perhaps it's the air quality, or something in the the Los Angeles water or perhaps SoFi Stadium itself, something is up in LA. The Rams, who now have placed another wide receiver on injured reserve, may agree SoFi stadium, the Chargers and Rams' shared stadium, has a role in this. Both Los Angeles teams are in the top 10 of most injured this season in nearly every metric. The Chargers emerge from the NFL trade deadline with the exact same roster and will now head to Baltimore to take on the Jacoby Brissett-led Ravens on Monday Night Football. The Chargers will have a chance to steal their first win of the season as the Ravens search for their identity with a brand new quarterback at the helm but will their long list of injuries get in the way? thursday's injury report for week 10 at BAL pic.twitter.com/fXSvi1MmEt It feels like groundhog day for the Chargers and their MASH unit of players following their loss to the Houston Texans. The Chargers have a significant portion of their cornerback room on the injury report. Tarheeb Still and Donte Jackson are the only cornerbacks not on the injury report to start the week of practice. The Chargers have had a revolving door at most positions on offense this season, which certainly has not helped their performance. The Baltimore Ravens tight end has been having a season to forget in 2026. His ninth season in the league, Andrews came into Nov. 16 with just 31 catches, 237 yards and a touchdown in nine games.
